# SiteKit

[English](https://github.com/dataarthub/sitekit/blob/main/README.md) | [日本語](https://github.com/dataarthub/sitekit/blob/main/README.ja.md)

[![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-blue?logo=typescript&style=flat)](https://www.typescriptlang.org/) [![Node.js 24+](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-24%2B-green?logo=nodedotjs&style=flat)](https://nodejs.org/) [![Astro](https://img.shields.io/badge/Astro-framework-purple?logo=astro&style=flat)](https://docs.astro.build/)

## Elevator Pitch

Astro developers use this framework to build static sites and basic content management around explicit content and hosting contracts.

## Why & Value Proposition

Configure an independent site using explicit content sources and standard hosting contracts.
Build from one pinned publication so content, media and generated pages share a revision.
Add public editing and storage adapters where needed; domain templates and advanced Studio integrations remain separate extensions.

## Key Highlights

- Validated site configuration with inline, file or HTTP content sources.
- Revision and image integrity checks before static rendering.
- Basic Markdown management with list/search, draft saving and publishing.
- Optional Cloudflare projection, analytics, commerce and editing adapters.

## Quickstart

Use Node.js 24+. Bun 1.4.0 is used for repository development and the commands below; installed consumers may use npm, pnpm or Yarn. These guides target the 0.2.0 release candidate. Until that version is confirmed readable from npm, start with its locally packed public core artifact from a verified source candidate. Appkit Core 0.2.1 / React 0.3.0 is available from npmjs when using the optional React screen.

```bash
bun add ./alneas-sitekit-0.2.0.tgz astro@^7.3.3
```

Save as `example.ts`, then run `bun example.ts`:

```typescript
import { defineSite } from '@alneas/sitekit/config';

const site = defineSite({
  id: 'example', revision: 1,
  content: { snapshot: { siteId: 'example', revision: 1, posts: [], assets: [] } },
});
console.log(site.id, site.revision); // example 1
```

# SiteKit Cloudflare Adapters

[English](https://github.com/dataarthub/sitekit/blob/main/packages/cloudflare/README.md) | [日本語](https://github.com/dataarthub/sitekit/blob/main/packages/cloudflare/README.ja.md)

[![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-blue?logo=typescript&style=flat)](https://www.typescriptlang.org/) [![Node.js 24+](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-24%2B-green?logo=nodedotjs&style=flat)](https://nodejs.org/) [![Cloudflare D1](https://img.shields.io/badge/Cloudflare-D1-orange?logo=cloudflare&style=flat)](https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/)

## Elevator Pitch

Site developers use these adapters to connect the framework's public site and editing contracts to Cloudflare storage and event services.

## Why & Value Proposition

Keep Cloudflare bindings and credentials outside browser code and the generic core.
Use D1/R2 projections as rebuildable read models when an upstream publishing system owns content.
Use the independent editing provider for host-owned content, with authentication and tenant authorization supplied explicitly by the server.

## Key Highlights

- Revisioned D1/R2 snapshot staging, promotion and rollback.
- D1 Markdown draft saving and publishing through an injected authorization boundary.
- Optional commerce, media, experiment and social outbox adapters.
- Queue and Analytics Engine event sinks.

## Quickstart

Use Node.js 24+. Bun 1.4.0 is used for repository development and the commands below; installed consumers may use npm, pnpm or Yarn. These examples target the 0.2.0 release candidate; until that version is confirmed readable from npm, install both local artifacts from the same verified source candidate. For the Worker example, configure a Queue producer binding named `ANALYTICS` and replace the example origin with your public site origin. The handler accepts validated POST batches at `/api/analytics`; the host owns abuse controls and downstream event processing. Queue acceptance does not establish downstream persistence. The origin allowlist is browser policy, not caller authentication.

```bash
bun add ./alneas-sitekit-cloudflare-0.2.0.tgz ./alneas-sitekit-0.2.0.tgz astro@^7.3.3
```

```typescript
import {
  createAnalyticsIngestHandler, createQueueAnalyticsIngestAdapter,
  type CloudflareAnalyticsQueue,
} from '@alneas/sitekit-cloudflare';

type Env = { ANALYTICS: CloudflareAnalyticsQueue };
const analytics = createAnalyticsIngestHandler<Env>({
  bindings: env => createQueueAnalyticsIngestAdapter(env.ANALYTICS),
  allowedOrigins: ['https://example.com'],
});

export default {
  fetch(request: Request, env: Env) {
    return analytics(request, env);
  },
};
```

## [FUNCTION] defineSite

Validates a site identity and exactly one content source.

### Signature

```typescript
import type { SiteDefinition } from '@alneas/sitekit/config';

declare function defineSite(input: SiteDefinition): SiteDefinition;
```

### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| input | SiteDefinition | Yes | Strict object containing id, optional revision, and content. |
| input.id | string | Yes | Nonempty string; trimmed by validation. |
| input.revision | number | No | Positive integer accepted by the schema. |
| input.content | { snapshot: unknown } \| { file: string; draftPreview?: boolean } \| { endpoint: string; method?: "GET" \| "POST" } | Yes | Exactly one source; file and endpoint must be nonempty. |

### Returns

`SiteDefinition` — the parsed configuration. Snapshot DTO validation occurs when the build loads content.

### Errors

Throws `SiteKitError` with code `SK_CONFIG_INVALID` for invalid configuration, extra fields or multiple sources. Endpoints require HTTPS; HTTP is allowed on loopback hosts. URL credentials are rejected. `draftPreview` applies only to files. Credentials belong in build options.

### Example

```typescript
import { defineSite } from '@alneas/sitekit/config';

const site = defineSite({
  id: 'example',
  revision: 1,
  content: { snapshot: { siteId: 'example', revision: 1, posts: [], assets: [] } },
});
console.log(site.id, site.revision); // example 1
```

## [FUNCTION] createSiteAstroConfig

Loads one publication, validates its identity and pins its images before configuring Astro.

### Signature

```typescript
import type { AstroUserConfig } from 'astro';
import type { SiteDefinition } from '@alneas/sitekit/config';
import type { SiteAstroConfigFactory, SiteBuildOptions } from '@alneas/sitekit/build';

declare function createSiteAstroConfig(
  input: SiteDefinition,
  configure: SiteAstroConfigFactory,
  options?: SiteBuildOptions,
): Promise<AstroUserConfig>;
```

### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| input | SiteDefinition | Yes | Site definition and optional expected revision. |
| configure | SiteAstroConfigFactory | Yes | Receives site, render snapshot and original publication; returns Astro configuration. |
| options.fetch | typeof fetch | No | Custom content and image fetch implementation. |
| options.headers | Record<string, string> | No | Build-only content request headers; never forwarded to image origins. |
| options.allowUnhashedImages | boolean | No | Migration compatibility; omitted by default. Does not bypass supplied hash checks. |

### Returns

`Promise<AstroUserConfig>` — static output by default, merged with the factory result and any image-pinning integration.

### Errors

Rejects missing or invalid content, site/revision mismatch, image retrieval failures and missing or mismatched image hashes. A snapshot declaring `imageIntegrity: "sha256"` rejects missing hashes even in compatibility mode. The factory receives a deeply frozen snapshot; `publication` preserves original image references for receipts. This function configures Astro; it does not run a build.

### Example

```typescript
import { defineSite } from '@alneas/sitekit/config';
import { createSiteAstroConfig } from '@alneas/sitekit/build';

const site = defineSite({
  id: 'example', revision: 1,
  content: { snapshot: { siteId: 'example', revision: 1, posts: [], assets: [] } },
});
const config = await createSiteAstroConfig(site, ({ snapshot }) => ({
  site: 'https://example.com',
  vite: { define: { PUBLIC_REVISION: JSON.stringify(snapshot.revision) } },
}));
console.log(config.output); // static
```

Configuration shape validation is available through the [JSON Schema data export](https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/guides/site-schema/). Runtime failures are documented in [error codes](https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/errors/); host callback errors are not reclassified.

---

Canonical guide: https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/cloudflare-api/
Source: `docs/cloudflare-api.md`

## [FUNCTION] parseCloudflareSnapshotManifest

Parses the structural fields of a snapshot manifest.

### Signature

```typescript
import type { SiteSnapshotManifest } from '@alneas/sitekit';

declare function parseCloudflareSnapshotManifest(value: unknown): SiteSnapshotManifest;
```

### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| value | unknown | Yes | Object to parse. |
| value.schemaVersion, value.siteId, value.revision | string | Yes | Nonempty strings. |
| value.generatedAt, value.contentVersion, value.mediaVersion, value.checksum | string | Yes | Nonempty strings; date and checksum formats are not checked here. |
| value.locales | string[] | Yes | Array of nonempty strings; an empty array is accepted. |
| value.signature | { algorithm: "hmac-sha256" \| "ed25519"; keyId: string; value: string } | No | Algorithm plus nonempty key identifier and signature value. |

### Returns

`SiteSnapshotManifest` — a new object containing recognized fields. Unrecognized fields are omitted.

### Errors and limits

Throws `Error` for invalid required fields or signature structure. This parser does not verify payload checksums, cryptographic signatures, supported schema versions or revision equality. Projection staging performs payload integrity checks separately. The example checksum is a structural placeholder and must not be used for staging.

### Example

```typescript
import { parseCloudflareSnapshotManifest } from '@alneas/sitekit-cloudflare';

const manifest = parseCloudflareSnapshotManifest({
  schemaVersion: '1', siteId: 'example', revision: 'cms-1',
  generatedAt: '2026-01-01T00:00:00Z',
  contentVersion: 'cms-1', mediaVersion: 'cms-1',
  checksum: 'example-checksum', locales: ['en', 'ja'],
});
console.log(manifest.revision); // cms-1
```

# Register a Section

## Prerequisites

Node.js 24+, Bun 1.4.0, a locally packed public core candidate and an existing Astro project. Install the schema dependency explicitly:

```bash
bun add ./alneas-sitekit-0.2.0.tgz astro zod
```

## Public import

Use `@alneas/sitekit/sections`; install the package name, not that subpath.
This framework-free registry needs no React provider or stylesheet.

## Step-by-Step Implementation

### 1. Define and resolve a plugin

Save as `section.ts`. The schema and component use the same section data type.

```typescript
import { z } from 'zod';
import { createSectionRegistry, defineSectionPlugin } from '@alneas/sitekit/sections';

const greeting = defineSectionPlugin({
  type: 'greeting',
  schema: z.object({ type: z.literal('greeting'), title: z.string() }),
  component: ({ section }) => section.data.title,
});
const registry = createSectionRegistry([greeting]);
const result = await registry.resolve(
  { id: 'welcome', type: 'greeting', data: { type: 'greeting', title: 'Hello' } },
  { siteId: 'example', locale: 'en', pathname: '/', collectionItems: {} },
);
console.log(result); // Hello
```

### 2. Run the section

```bash
bun section.ts
```

## Verification

Expected output:

```text
Hello
```

This verifies registry resolution. An Astro renderer must consume the resolved value to display it on a page.

## Troubleshooting / Common Pitfalls

- Duplicate section names fail registration. Choose a unique plugin type.
- Unknown types fail resolution. Register the plugin before resolving content.
- Invalid data fails schema parsing. Keep the node type and schema literal consistent.
- Legacy names can use explicit registry aliases; the canonical plugin must already be registered.

See [architecture](https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/architecture/) for the reason renderer-specific domain branches stay outside the registry.

---

Canonical guide: https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/tutorials/first-site/
Source: `docs/tutorials/first-site.md`

# Your First Site Configuration

In about five minutes, validate a site configuration without a CMS or deployment. Use Node.js 24+, Bun 1.4.0 and the locally packed public core artifact from a verified source candidate. These examples target 0.2.0; confirm registry availability before using versioned npm dependencies. Examples use fictional identifiers and reserved example domains.

## Public import

Configuration uses `@alneas/sitekit/config`. It needs no React runtime, provider or CSS. The installation below installs the package artifact; `/config` is an import target.

## 1. Create a project

```bash
mkdir site-demo
cd site-demo
bun init -y
```

Expected result: Bun creates `package.json` and the starter project files.

## 2. Install the framework

Place the packed core artifact beside the new `site-demo` directory, then run:

```bash
bun add ../alneas-sitekit-0.2.0.tgz astro
```

Expected result: Bun reports both packages installed and writes the lockfile.

## 3. Save the configuration

Create `example.ts` with this content:

```typescript
import { defineSite } from '@alneas/sitekit/config';

const site = defineSite({
  id: 'example',
  revision: 1,
  content: { snapshot: { siteId: 'example', revision: 1, posts: [], assets: [] } },
});
console.log(site.id, site.revision); // example 1
```

Expected result: `example.ts` contains the inline snapshot and matching site identity.

## 4. Run it

```bash
bun example.ts
```

Expected output:

```text
example 1
```

You now have a validated site configuration. This exercise validates configuration only; rendering pages requires Astro pages and the build entry point documented in the [API reference](https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/api/).

Canonical guide: https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/architecture/
Source: `docs/architecture.md`

# SiteKit Architecture

## Motivation

A site should keep the same content contracts when its CMS or hosting changes. The public core therefore owns configuration, normalized content/media, sections and build inputs. Hosts choose a publishing authority, authentication and deployment separately.

Each build reads one publication. Its identity, expected revision and image bytes are checked before page rendering, preventing a mixture of content and media revisions. Inline snapshots, files and HTTP endpoints share this path.

## Architectural Diagram

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Source[Inline / file / HTTP publication] --> Build[Validate identity, revision and images]
  Build --> Core[Public site and section contracts]
  Core --> Pages[Consumer Astro pages]
  Pages --> Static[Static HTML and machine-readable outputs]
  Admin[Public basic Markdown management] --> HTTP[Same-origin HTTP client]
  HTTP --> Auth[Host authentication and tenant authorization]
  Auth --> Edit[Optional D1 editing provider]
  Edit --> Content[Host-owned content]
  Source --> Projection[Optional revisioned D1/R2 read model]
  Extensions[Optional domain templates and advanced Studio] --> Core
```

## Trade-offs & Decisions

### Integration terms

EAOS is an optional external content-management ecosystem supported by compatibility contracts; an independent SiteKit site does not require its account or SDK. In extension documentation, private means a separately distributed implementation. A content record whose visibility is `private` instead describes delivery policy; it is not a package dependency. Generic public schema SQL provisions a consumer-owned database and contains no production/customer database contents.

### One content authority

Upstream-managed content and rebuildable projections are different responsibilities. When a publishing system owns content, its D1/R2 projection must not become a competing editor. An independent host can instead select its own D1 authoring provider. The editing provider marks document states; it does not trigger a production deployment or manufacture a publication snapshot.

### Useful basic management with separate advanced extensions

The public screen supplies list/search, Markdown fields, draft saving and publishing. Its host injects persistence and server authorization. The private wrapper can supply a richer editor without changing the public screen. Advanced editing, integrated campaign/experiment/social dashboards and domain-specific presentation remain outside the public candidate. Basic usability is not intentionally withheld to create an upgrade requirement.

### Static pages with explicit server boundaries

The default site output is static. Editing, payments and analytics require explicit server handlers and bindings. Browser imports must not load database SDKs, filesystem access or backend credentials. Provider contracts allow a host to replace an adapter without duplicating the build system.

### Image integrity versus migration compatibility

Rendering uses locally pinned, verified image bytes. Build authentication headers are not forwarded to media origins. The original publication remains available for receipt comparison. A compatibility option can accept older publications without hashes, but supplied hashes are still checked and a publication declaring SHA-256 integrity cannot use that exception.

### Metadata is not authorization

Visibility and offer metadata are portable contracts. AI projection can omit restricted bodies while retaining metadata; search can include restricted records unless the host filters them. Neither operation grants access. Authenticate users and enforce access before returning content or creating a build intended for a narrower audience.

### Documentation ownership

This project owns the English source guides, examples, public import declarations and JSDoc. Package READMEs stay plain Markdown; a small local script adds metadata to generated landing documents. `docs.manifest.json` selects the exact documents and source entrypoints available to the downstream portal.

The portal owns navigation, rendering, translations and generated API presentation. Its verify-only importer can check this project's manifest without importing or publishing it. Internal plans, customer/operator evidence, credentials and historical archives are outside the public manifest. See [extension boundaries](https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/extensions/) and [source verification](https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/guides/verify-source/).

# Use public Studio integrations

## Prerequisites

Use Node.js 24 or later. The optional React table requires React and React DOM
matching `^19.2.3`. Obtain the framework and Cloudflare artifacts from the same
verified source candidate. This repository's packages are local release candidates;
Appkit Core 0.2.2 / React 0.3.1 is published on npmjs.

```bash
bun add ./alneas-sitekit-0.2.0.tgz ./alneas-sitekit-cloudflare-0.2.0.tgz
bun add --exact --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org @alneas/appkit-core@0.2.2 @alneas/appkit-react@0.3.1 react@19.2.3 react-dom@19.2.3
```

For a server-only adapter, install just Appkit Core and the Cloudflare artifact
alongside the framework. The framework's React/Appkit React peers are optional.
Install package names; the subpaths below are import targets.

## Public import

| Feature | Published package subpath in the candidate |
| --- | --- |
| Basic management screen | `@alneas/sitekit/studio/basic` |
| Browser HTTP provider | `@alneas/sitekit/studio/http-provider` |
| Basic screen styles | `@alneas/sitekit/studio/basic.css` |
| Host Studio contracts | `@alneas/sitekit/studio/contracts` (types) |
| Access/body metadata conversion | `@alneas/sitekit/studio/content-metadata` |
| Optional collection table | `@alneas/sitekit/studio/collection-list` |
| D1 editing provider | `@alneas/sitekit-cloudflare/studio` |
| Editing HTTP handler | `@alneas/sitekit-cloudflare/studio-handler` |
| Upstream content contracts | `@alneas/appkit-core/data/content` (types) |
| Upstream table and stylesheet | `@alneas/appkit-react/tools/data-table`, `@alneas/appkit-react/styles` |

The full `./studio` UI barrel and `./site-studio` are excluded from the public
framework candidate. They still require restricted UI. The subpaths in this table
have separate exports and do not load that barrel.

## Step-by-Step Implementation

### 1. Mount the basic management screen

The public screen includes list/search, create, Markdown editing, draft save and
publish. It uses the public Appkit table and ordinary accessible form controls.
The full rich editor, integrated analytics, experiments and social publishing UI
remain outside the public candidate.

Import all styles once at the application boundary. Create a stable provider and
save the following component as `src/components/ContentAdmin.tsx`:

```tsx
import '@alneas/appkit-react/styles';
import '@alneas/sitekit/studio/basic.css';
import { BasicStudioApp } from '@alneas/sitekit/studio/basic';
import { createHttpStudioProvider } from '@alneas/sitekit/studio/http-provider';

const provider = createHttpStudioProvider();
export function ContentAdmin() {
  return <BasicStudioApp provider={provider} collections={[{ id: 'posts', label: '記事' }]} />;
}
```

For an Astro host, enable its React renderer before mounting the component. Run
this in the consuming Astro project and accept the integration's setup prompts:

```bash
bunx astro add react
```

The [official Astro React integration guide](https://docs.astro.build/en/guides/integrations-guide/react/)
describes installation and configuration. Preserve the host's existing integrations
and snapshot build configuration. Create `src/pages/admin.astro` with:

```astro
---
import { ContentAdmin } from '../components/ContentAdmin';
---
<html lang="en">
  <head><title>Content management</title></head>
  <body><ContentAdmin client:only="react" /></body>
</html>
```

The page mounts the client screen at `/admin`; it does not create or secure an API.
Mount the server handler from the next section at `/api/studio/content`, implement
its authentication/authorization callbacks, and apply the D1 schema explicitly.
The client uses same-origin cookie credentials. Custom session handling can be
provided through the client's `fetch` option; never put backend credentials in
client modules. Saving sends the document's previous `modifiedAt` for conflict
checking. Storage failures preserve the entered content for retry. Returning to
the list asks before discarding unsaved edits. Publish saves the current draft
first, so a newly created document can be published directly.

After installing the source candidate, run `bun scripts/public-consumer-smoke.mjs --preview` to launch the isolated tarball-based acceptance fixture at loopback.
It uses a temporary SQLite database implementing D1's statement interface and a
local fixture session. The seed, simulated error control and fixture session are
for local verification only; do not deploy this preview server as production auth.

### 2. Use a collection table separately

Import the stylesheet once at the application boundary. Use a browser bundler
supporting dynamic imports and React. No query or data-access provider is needed
by this table wrapper; the host supplies the items and handlers.

```tsx
import '@alneas/appkit-react/styles';
import { ReactToolsCollectionList } from '@alneas/sitekit/studio/collection-list';

export function ContentList() {
  return (
    <ReactToolsCollectionList
      items={[]}
      loading={false}
      onSelect={item => console.log(item.id)}
      onCreate={() => console.log('Create draft')}
      fallback={<p>Loading content…</p>}
    />
  );
}
```

The fallback appears during loading, server rendering or a failed optional table
load. Reuse the same compatible React runtime in the host and Appkit.

### 3. Connect D1 editing on the server

Supply the D1 binding, apply `contentStudioSchemaSql` from the Cloudflare root
entry to your selected database, and configure the host's authentication and
collection/tenant authorization before mounting an editing endpoint. Schema
application and persistence writes are explicit host operations.

This minimal example denies all requests until the host supplies its policy:

```typescript
import { createD1ContentStudioProvider } from '@alneas/sitekit-cloudflare/studio';
import { createContentStudioHandler } from '@alneas/sitekit-cloudflare/studio-handler';
import type { CloudflareD1Database } from '@alneas/sitekit-cloudflare';

export const handleStudio = createContentStudioHandler<{ DB: CloudflareD1Database }>({
  bindings: env => createD1ContentStudioProvider({ database: env.DB }),
  authorize: () => false,
});
```

Mount `handleStudio(request, env)` at `/api/studio/content`. The example returns
403 before touching the database. For a multi-tenant host, use authenticated
principal data to scope provider bindings and authorize both reads and writes;
never derive tenant access solely from request input. Keep D1 bindings and
credentials in server modules.

## Verification

Run the framework's `typecheck:all`, `test:all`, `verify:public` and `test:consumer`
commands in the generated candidate. The isolated consumer checks the new exports,
table fallback, a denied request, and create/update/publish using the actual schema in an isolated SQLite database. Test real editing
with a host-owned test database and authentication setup before enabling it.

## Troubleshooting / Common Pitfalls

A missing full Studio/editor export is an expected distribution boundary. The
public Core editor helpers do not supply the restricted BlockNote React editor.

For exact signatures and request/response contracts, see the [Studio API](https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/studio-api/).

---

Canonical guide: https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/tutorials/basic-admin/
Source: `docs/tutorials/basic-admin.md`

# Try Basic Content Management

In about five minutes, manage a test article in an isolated local browser fixture. Use Node.js 24+, Bun 1.4.0, npmjs connectivity and an extracted public source candidate. Start a terminal in that candidate's root. No private registry or CMS credentials are required.

## Public import

The fixture consumes the core `/studio/basic`, `/studio/http-provider` and `/studio/basic.css` exports plus the Cloudflare `/studio` and `/studio-handler` exports. Package names are listed in the [exports reference](https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/exports/). This React example shows the actual browser imports used by the fixture:

```tsx
import '@alneas/appkit-react/styles';
import '@alneas/sitekit/studio/basic.css';
import { BasicStudioApp } from '@alneas/sitekit/studio/basic';
import { createHttpStudioProvider } from '@alneas/sitekit/studio/http-provider';
const provider = createHttpStudioProvider();
export function Admin() {
  return <BasicStudioApp provider={provider} collections={[{ id: 'posts', label: 'Posts' }]} />;
}
```

## 1. Install the locked dependencies

```bash
bun install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org
```

Expected result: the candidate's locked public dependencies are installed.

## 2. Start the local fixture

```bash
bun scripts/public-consumer-smoke.mjs --preview
```

Expected result: the script packs both framework packages, installs them in an isolated consumer with npmjs Appkit, checks the actual SQLite schema and HTTP path, then prints `Basic Studio preview: http://127.0.0.1:4317/`.

## 3. Create an article

Open the printed URL. Select **新規作成**, enter a title and slug, and write Markdown in the body field. Leave summary and tags empty. Select **下書き保存**.

Expected result: **下書きを保存しました** appears. Return to the list and open the article using its title button. The entered values remain.

## 4. Publish and reopen

Select **公開**, then reload the page.

Expected result: **公開しました** appears before reloading, and the list shows the article's **公開** state afterwards. This changes the temporary fixture record; it does not publish a website to the Internet.

## 5. Finish

Stop the terminal process with Ctrl-C. The fixture uses a temporary SQLite database and a local test session; neither is a production authentication setup. You have verified the basic public management flow. Follow the [integration guide](https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/guides/public-studio/) to connect your own authenticated server and D1 binding.

---

Canonical guide: https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/studio-api/
Source: `docs/studio-api.md`

# Studio API

## Public import

Install package names as described in the [integration guide](https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/guides/public-studio/). The table in [public exports](https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/exports/) is the supported import surface. Node.js 24+ is required; React UI requires React/React DOM `^19.2.3` and both `@alneas/appkit-react/styles` and `/studio/basic.css`. HTTP clients run in the browser; D1 bindings and authorization stay on the server.

## [FUNCTION] BasicStudioApp

Renders list/search, Markdown editing, draft saving and publishing through a host provider.

```typescript
import type { JSX } from 'react';
import type { BasicStudioAppProps } from '@alneas/sitekit/studio/basic';
declare function BasicStudioApp(props: BasicStudioAppProps): JSX.Element;
```

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| props.provider | StudioProvider | Yes | Stable host adapter implementing list/get/saveDraft/publish. |
| props.collections | readonly StudioCollectionDefinition[] | Yes | Host-selected collection IDs, labels and optional draft factories. |
| props.initialCollection | string | No | Selected collection; defaults to the first. |
| props.initialLocale | string | No | Defaults to `ja`; built-in selector exposes `ja` and `en`. |
| props.title | string | No | Defaults to `Content Studio`. |
| props.renderBodyEditor | (props: StudioBodyEditorProps) => ReactNode | No | Replaces the default Markdown textarea. |
| props.renderCollectionList | (props: StudioCollectionListProps) => ReactNode | No | Fallback while Appkit table loading/failure is active. |
| props.renderMetadataEditor | (props: StudioMetadataEditorProps) => ReactNode | No | Replaces title/slug/summary/tag fields. |

**Returns:** a React element. Provider work starts on the client. The screen catches listing/open/save/publish errors and keeps entered content when saving fails. Publish saves the current draft first. This is basic management, without rendering previews, deletion, media picking or revision history.

```tsx
import '@alneas/appkit-react/styles';
import '@alneas/sitekit/studio/basic.css';
import { BasicStudioApp } from '@alneas/sitekit/studio/basic';
import { createHttpStudioProvider } from '@alneas/sitekit/studio/http-provider';
const provider = createHttpStudioProvider();
export function Admin() {
  return <BasicStudioApp provider={provider} collections={[{ id: 'posts', label: 'Posts' }]} />;
}
```

## [FUNCTION] createHttpStudioProvider

Creates a same-origin browser adapter for the editing endpoint.

```typescript
import type { HttpStudioProviderOptions } from '@alneas/sitekit/studio/http-provider';
import type { StudioProvider } from '@alneas/sitekit/studio/contracts';
declare function createHttpStudioProvider(options?: HttpStudioProviderOptions): StudioProvider;
```

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| options.endpoint | string | No | Defaults to `/api/studio/content`; requires a same-origin absolute path without query/fragment/backslash. |
| options.fetch | typeof fetch | No | Custom authenticated fetch wrapper. |

**Returns:** a `StudioProvider` implementing list/get/saveDraft/publish, with `credentials: 'same-origin'` and `cache: 'no-store'`. Non-2xx, network and JSON errors reject. Unsupported advanced methods are absent. Construction rejects an invalid endpoint.

```typescript
import { createHttpStudioProvider } from '@alneas/sitekit/studio/http-provider';
const provider = createHttpStudioProvider();
// Run from an authenticated browser with a mounted editing handler.
const page = await provider.list({ collection: 'posts', locale: 'en' });
console.log(page.items.length);
```

## [FUNCTION] createD1ContentStudioProvider

Creates a D1 authoring adapter for the shared public content contract.

```typescript
import type { ContentStudioProvider } from '@alneas/appkit-core/data/content';
import type { D1ContentStudioProviderOptions } from '@alneas/sitekit-cloudflare/studio';
declare function createD1ContentStudioProvider(options: D1ContentStudioProviderOptions): ContentStudioProvider;
```

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| options.database | CloudflareD1Database | Yes | Server-only D1 binding; apply `contentStudioSchemaSql` explicitly. |
| options.table | string | No | Defaults to `content_items`; identifier validation is applied. |
| options.tenantField | string | No | Optional tenant column name. |
| options.tenantId | string | No | Enables scoping only when paired with tenantField. |

**Returns:** a provider with list/get/saveDraft/publish. List limits are clamped to 1–100 with cursor pagination. Draft saves write `draft` state; `expectedModifiedAt` is a pre-write check, not an atomic compare-and-swap. Publish marks `published`, or `scheduled` when requested; no scheduler or deployment runs here. Database failures reject.

```typescript
import { createD1ContentStudioProvider } from '@alneas/sitekit-cloudflare/studio';
import type { CloudflareD1Database } from '@alneas/sitekit-cloudflare';
export function connect(database: CloudflareD1Database) {
  return createD1ContentStudioProvider({ database });
}
```

## [FUNCTION] createContentStudioHandler

Creates the server request handler with host-injected authentication, authorization and bindings.

```typescript
import type { ContentStudioHandler, ContentStudioHandlerOptions } from '@alneas/sitekit-cloudflare/studio-handler';
declare function createContentStudioHandler<TEnv>(options: ContentStudioHandlerOptions<TEnv>): ContentStudioHandler<TEnv>;
```

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| options.bindings | (env, principal?) => ContentStudioProvider | Yes | Resolves a provider after authorization. |
| options.authorize | (context) => boolean \| Promise<boolean> | Yes | Must return exactly true for access; distinguish read/write and enforce tenant/collection rules. |
| options.authenticate | (context) => principal \| null \| Promise<principal \| null> | No | When supplied, a missing principal produces 401. |
| options.path | string | No | Defaults to `/api/studio/content`. |
| options.maxRequestBytes | number | No | Defaults to 256 KiB, including streamed POST bodies. |
| options.allowedOrigins | readonly string[] | No | Explicit CORS origins. An empty list does not supply authentication or a CSRF policy. |

**Returns:** `(request, env) => Promise<Response>`. The example denies all access until a host policy is connected. `ContentStudioPrincipal` contains subject, tenantId and roles; the handler does not verify credentials itself.

```typescript
import { createContentStudioHandler } from '@alneas/sitekit-cloudflare/studio-handler';
import { createD1ContentStudioProvider } from '@alneas/sitekit-cloudflare/studio';
import type { CloudflareD1Database } from '@alneas/sitekit-cloudflare';
export const handle = createContentStudioHandler<{ DB: CloudflareD1Database }>({
  bindings: env => createD1ContentStudioProvider({ database: env.DB }),
  authorize: () => false,
});
```

## [GET] /api/studio/content

Lists collection documents, or loads one document when `id` is supplied.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| id | string | No | Returns `{ document }`, where document may be null. |
| collection | string | Yes for listing | Collection identifier. |
| locale, search, status | string | No | Provider filters; status supports draft/scheduled/published/archived/all. |
| limit | number | No | Integer from 1 to 100; the handler rejects values outside that range. |
| cursor | string | No | Opaque cursor returned by the provider. |

**Returns:** 200 with `{ items, nextCursor? }` or `{ document }`. See the HTTP client example above for a complete public call.

## [POST] /api/studio/content

Saves a draft or changes a document's publish state.

| Body property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| operation | "saveDraft" \| "publish" | Yes | Selects the operation. |
| document | ContentStudioDocument | For saveDraft | Collection, locale, slug, title, body, tags and data; an empty summary is accepted. |
| documentId | string | For publish | Assigned document identifier. |
| options | save/publish options | No | expectedModifiedAt/reason or scheduledAt/reason. |

**Returns:** 200 with `{ document }`. Errors: 400 invalid input/operation, 401 missing authentication, 403 denied access/origin, 404 wrong path, 405 wrong method, 413 oversized body, 500 provider failure. A stale-draft provider rejection is currently a provider failure, not a dedicated 409 conflict response.

```typescript
import { createHttpStudioProvider } from '@alneas/sitekit/studio/http-provider';
const provider = createHttpStudioProvider();
const saved = await provider.saveDraft({ id: '', collection: 'posts', locale: 'en',
  slug: 'hello', title: 'Hello', body: '# Hello', summary: '', tags: [], data: {} });
console.log((await provider.publish(saved.id)).status);
```

## [INTERFACE] StudioProvider

The host management boundary; import it from `/studio/contracts`.

```typescript
import type { ContentItem, MediaAsset } from '@alneas/sitekit/contracts';
import type { StudioListQuery, StudioListResult, StudioSaveOptions, StudioPublishOptions, StudioRevision } from '@alneas/sitekit/studio/contracts';
interface StudioProvider {
  list(query: StudioListQuery): Promise<StudioListResult>;
  get(documentId: string): Promise<ContentItem | null>;
  saveDraft(document: ContentItem, options?: StudioSaveOptions): Promise<ContentItem>;
  publish(documentId: string, options?: StudioPublishOptions): Promise<ContentItem>;
  listRevisions?(documentId: string): Promise<StudioRevision[]>;
  listMedia?(query?: { search?: string; limit?: number }): Promise<MediaAsset[]>;
}
```

**Parameters/returns:** each method receives the query or document shown in the signature and resolves its declared result. Optional history/media methods are extension points; the basic screen does not call them. The public HTTP client is a self-contained implementation example above.

Metadata conversion helpers and the optional collection-table entry are documented in source JSDoc at their [public imports](https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/exports/). Generated API presentation belongs to the downstream portal; source signatures and examples remain canonical here.

---

Canonical guide: https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/exports/
Source: `docs/exports.md`

A package subpath is an import target, not a separately installable package.

```bash
bun add ./alneas-sitekit-0.2.0.tgz ./alneas-sitekit-cloudflare-0.2.0.tgz astro
```

## Peers, styles and providers

| Feature | Requirements |
| --- | --- |
| Core configuration/build | Node.js 24+, Astro peer, Bun for the documented candidate scripts. |
| Basic React screen | React and React DOM ^19.2.3, public Appkit React 0.3.1; one compatible React instance. |
| Basic screen styling | `@alneas/appkit-react/styles` and core `/studio/basic.css`. |
| Standalone collection table | Public Appkit stylesheet; no query/data-access provider needed. |
| HTTP editing | Stable `StudioProvider`, same-origin endpoint and a server-enforced authentication/authorization policy. |
| D1 editing | Public Appkit Core 0.2.2 types, provisioned `contentStudioSchemaSql`, server D1 binding. |
| Other adapters | Host-supplied D1/R2, HTTP clients, payment verifiers or event sinks described by the selected API. |

## Exclusions

The full `/studio` barrel, `/site-studio`, restricted editor, domain templates/themes and Platform/operator integrations are outside this public surface. Source availability alone does not establish an exported or published path. Advanced capabilities are separate [extension boundaries](https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/extensions/).

See the [site API](https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/api/), [manifest API](https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/cloudflare-api/), [Studio API](https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/studio-api/) and [integration guide](https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/guides/public-studio/). Detailed function/type descriptions live in source JSDoc for the portal's downstream API extraction; this project does not maintain a second portal renderer.

## Connection contracts

`@alneas/sitekit/connection` exports credential-free connection metadata,
portable template descriptors and their runtime parsers. See
[Connection and template contracts](https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/guides/connection-contracts/).

The `@alneas/sitekit/management` entry supplies credential-free settings contracts, strict parsers and the shared save/apply policy over host-owned persistence and authorization. See [shared management settings](https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/guides/management-settings/).

Shared management surfaces: `@alneas/sitekit/management/http`, `@alneas/sitekit/management/react`, `@alneas/sitekit/management/styles.css`, and `@alneas/sitekit-cloudflare/management`. See [Embed the Shared Management Console](https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/guides/management-console/).

Canonical guide: https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/extensions/
Source: `docs/extensions.md`

# Public Foundations and Optional Extensions

## Motivation

An independent site must be configurable and its basic content manageable without a private CMS SDK. At the same time, a reusable hotel experience or integrated operational dashboard can be a separate product. Technical availability in a public dependency does not automatically make every composition part of this framework's public scope.

## Architectural Diagram

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Public[Public configuration, build and basic Markdown management] --> Provider[Host-owned providers and renderers]
  Provider --> Adapter[Public D1/R2 and HTTP adapters]
  Provider --> Domain[Optional domain templates and booking presentation]
  Provider --> Advanced[Optional rich editor and advanced Studio]
```

## Trade-offs & Decisions

| Public foundation | Optional extension boundary |
| --- | --- |
| Configuration, publication loading and static build | Domain-specific routes, layouts and complete visual presets |
| Basic list/search, Markdown editing, draft save and publish | Rich block editing and integrated operational workflows |
| Host/provider interfaces and metadata conversion | Integrated analytics, experiments and social publishing UI |
| Generic persistence/event adapters | Host-specific operational composition and deployment tooling |

The public contract leaves room for paid extensions. Product scope, pricing and availability are not established by this guide. Generic adapters are integration primitives, not a promise of a complete operational service.

The public package does not export the full legacy Studio barrel, Site Studio or restricted BlockNote wrapper. Use the documented [public subpaths](https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/exports/); a source directory or an old package name does not imply a supported import.

For basic management, use the [tutorial](https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/tutorials/basic-admin/) or [integration guide](https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/guides/public-studio/). Production authentication, tenant authorization and deployment remain host responsibilities. These extension boundaries are distinct from confidential material: customer data, credentials, operator receipts and unreviewed dependency archives are never public documentation inputs.

---

Canonical guide: https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/guides/verify-source/
Source: `docs/guides/verify-source.md`

# Verify the Source Candidate

## Prerequisites

Bun 1.4.0, Node.js 24 or later, access to the public npm registry, and an extracted source candidate. No private registry or CMS credentials are required.

## Public import

The checks consume the package names and subpaths documented in the [public export reference](https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/exports/). No private SDK or credentials are required. A minimal runtime import is:

```typescript
import { defineSite } from '@alneas/sitekit/config';
console.log(defineSite({ id: 'example', content: { snapshot: { siteId: 'example', revision: 1, posts: [], assets: [] } } }).id);
```

## Step-by-Step Implementation

### 1. Install the locked dependencies

Run from the extracted project root:

```bash
bun install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org
```

### 2. Validate the source boundary and packages

```bash
bun run verify:public
bun run typecheck:all
bun run docs:check
bun run test:all
bun run build:all
```

### 3. Verify builds and isolated package installation

```bash
bun run test:site-build
bun run test:consumer
```

### 4. Pack artifacts for the quickstarts

From the candidate root, put archives outside the checkout:

```bash
artifact_dir=$(mktemp -d)
bun pm pack --cwd packages/core --ignore-scripts --filename "$artifact_dir/alneas-sitekit-0.2.0.tgz"
bun pm pack --cwd packages/cloudflare --ignore-scripts --filename "$artifact_dir/alneas-sitekit-cloudflare-0.2.0.tgz"
```

Expected result: both tarballs exist in `$artifact_dir`; packing does not publish them. Copy the selected archives into a separate disposable consumer directory to use the quickstarts' `bun add ./alneas-sitekit-0.2.0.tgz` commands, or pass their absolute paths to `bun add`. Do not place archives in the checkout or commit them. Remove the temporary archives after verification.

These are development candidates. For a committed release candidate, use the [release guide](https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/guides/release/) to prepare and validate a commit-bound bundle instead.

## Verification

The boundary check reports registered documentation, publishable package configuration and the required full release validation hook. The tests cover the generic core and adapter. The build smoke test produces equivalent static HTML from inline, file and HTTP inputs, with verified image bytes. The consumer test packs both packages, checks their MIT license files, installs them into a temporary project and imports their public entry points, including the basic management screen, HTTP client, Studio contracts, metadata, the collection table and Cloudflare editing APIs. SQLite persistence is checked with the actual public schema. The optional table requires compatible React peers and the Appkit stylesheet; see [public Studio integrations](https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/guides/public-studio/).

## Troubleshooting / Common Pitfalls

- Dependency download failures: check public npm connectivity and Bun's writable temporary/cache directories.
- Image mismatch or missing hash: correct the publication and image bytes together; do not disable verification.
- A private-file boundary failure: keep operator records, proprietary integrations and dependency archives outside the source candidate.
- Package publication fails during validation: correct the reported boundary, dependency, documentation, build or test failure, then rerun the gate. The workspace root remains private; select one of the two publishable packages.

## Maintainer documentation checks

`bun run docs:prepare` wraps the canonical plain READMEs in metadata-bearing landing documents. `bun run docs:check` runs `test:jsdoc`, builds declarations, checks the explicit public manifest, validates feature imports against the selected package exports, and typechecks guide/JSDoc examples as ESM with Astro-style bundler resolution. JSDoc coverage follows canonical declarations reachable through the approved exports, including nested members, callbacks, overloads, type parameters and constraints, and inferred return types inside containers. Re-exported contracts are checked once; private and protected class members and unrelated implementation locals are excluded. Summaries and callable parameter, result and example tags are required at the owning contract. Regression tests exercise missing contracts and valid examples; structural coverage cannot establish that prose accurately describes behavior, so review descriptions against implementation and existing behavior tests. Stylesheet imports are validated against exports; bundling is checked separately by the consumer test.

The source candidate contains no documentation website or translation runtime. Run the downstream portal's importer with `--verify` against this project's manifest when its checkout is available; that read-only preflight is separate from actual ingestion and publication. Edit sources here, not generated portal pages.

## Content, authority and lifecycle assessment

`bun run test:contracts` executes the required content/build, access/AI, stored
projection and Studio handler contracts. Its JSON report must contain every
selected file, with nonempty tests and no skipped, todo or failed assertions.
The runner's regression executes real empty and skip-only fixtures and rejects
both. The gate runs before `release:check` and the source selector retains it for
source, test and shared helper changes. It supplements the full suites and packed
consumers; it does not certify every development-policy clause. The installed
policy catalog predates the current coding and lifecycle additions.

For coding and adapter reuse, generic content/checksum contracts remain in Core;
D1/R2 persistence remains in Cloudflare. Studio uses the existing Appkit provider
contract, and EAOS publication uses the existing compatibility adapter. No new
provider connection is introduced. Public dependency/import inspection and packed
consumers remain required; declarations alone do not prove a provider's behavior.

Publication tests bind the site, revision and image bytes before rendering. Stored
projection reads now require both content and media objects to match the selected
manifest checksum. Promoting an empty replacement revision removes those records
from current-head reads without changing another site. Explicitly pinned older
revisions remain readable, and restaging the same revision is supported; hosts
must control these administrative operations. Separate D1/R2 writes are not an
atomic transaction. Existing readers, built pages, media URLs, search/AI indexes,
previews and external caches require host-owned rebuild, purge and access controls;
the tests do not prove delivery-wide withdrawal. AI helpers omit restricted body
text but retain descriptive metadata and do not check publication status; hosts
must apply the access decision before projecting unpublished content.

Tenant tests cover the projection's site/revision lookup boundary and Studio's
injected host authority. They do not establish tenant isolation for external
search/vector indexes, jobs, exports, signed links, backups or offboarding. Studio
origin controls do not authenticate callers. Hosts own identity verification,
provider tenant scoping and revocation. There is no model/MCP execution engine or
approval-token protocol here; replay/revision-bound approvals belong to the
executing host, not a content document.

Durable adapters have local tests, but this gate does not establish exactly-once
external effects, restart recovery, deduplication retention, quarantine/replay
ownership or plugin suspension. Hosts must verify those operational contracts.
AI representations make no model calls: approved destinations, retention, fallback
and retry/delegation budgets are host responsibilities and are unverified here.

No dedicated vulnerability reporting/triage contract is declared in this source
candidate; maintainer ownership, advisory handling, supported-version fix delivery
and expiring exceptions remain unverified. Node 24/26
and packed-consumer checks cover declared source compatibility; provider versions,
persisted-data migration, deprecation/removal and security-fix support need owner
review. Rollback selects retained revisions; it is not tested backup restoration,
a recovery-time/data-loss guarantee or a production migration. Domain, security,
data, API and CI review ownership and consequential decisions require maintainer
review; local tests and workflow declarations do not establish branch-protection
or human-approval enforcement. No production, live-provider or restore operation
is performed by these checks.

---

Canonical guide: https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/guides/content-sources/
Source: `docs/guides/content-sources.md`

# Build from independent or managed content

## Prerequisites

A site using Astro 7.3.3 or later within major 7, the core package, and a public snapshot matching the [configuration API](https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/api/). This guide targets the 0.2.0 release candidate; the published 0.1.0 package does not include all APIs shown here. Confirm 0.2.0 registry availability before adoption. For local verification, use the [source verification guide](https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/guides/verify-source/).

## Public import

Use `@alneas/sitekit/config` and `@alneas/sitekit/build` from the core package. These are Node/Astro build entry points; they do not run in the browser. The following examples include both imports.

## Step-by-Step Implementation

### Independent site

Keep your own repository. In astro.config.mjs, pass exactly one snapshot source: an in-memory snapshot, a local snapshot file, or an HTTP endpoint.

```javascript
import { defineSite } from '@alneas/sitekit/config';
import { createSiteAstroConfig } from '@alneas/sitekit/build';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

export default await createSiteAstroConfig(defineSite({
  id: 'example',
  revision: 1,
  content: { file: fileURLToPath(new URL('./snapshot.json', import.meta.url)) },
}), ({ snapshot }) => ({
  site: 'https://example.com',
  vite: { define: { __SITE_SNAPSHOT__: JSON.stringify(snapshot) } },
}));
```

Add ordinary Astro pages that render the pinned snapshot. No EAOS account, API credentials or Cloudflare bindings are required for a file build.

### Managed site or independent CMS

Use the same build function with an HTTP source. The endpoint must provide one pinned public revision; the builder rejects mismatched site identity or revision.

```javascript
import { defineSite } from '@alneas/sitekit/config';
import { createSiteAstroConfig } from '@alneas/sitekit/build';

export default await createSiteAstroConfig(defineSite({
  id: 'example', revision: 1,
  content: { endpoint: process.env.SITE_SNAPSHOT_URL, method: 'GET' },
}), ({ snapshot }) => ({
  site: 'https://example.com',
  vite: { define: { __SITE_SNAPSHOT__: JSON.stringify(snapshot) } },
}), {
  headers: process.env.SITE_BUILD_TOKEN
    ? { Authorization: 'Bearer ' + process.env.SITE_BUILD_TOKEN }
    : {},
});
```

Configure SITE_SNAPSHOT_URL and, only when required by your host, SITE_BUILD_TOKEN as build secrets. A service requiring POST may use method:'POST'. Credentials are build options, never snapshot content or browser configuration. Do not put private drafts or secrets into the public snapshot; the example deliberately embeds its public content in the generated site.

EAOS-managed sites may share one execution repository and use registered site settings, package versions and Deploy Hooks. Independent sites own their repository and deployment pipeline. The core build API stays the same. D1/R2 or ADB/OCI are upstream CMS/storage choices; the builder reads HTTP snapshots and verifies image bytes instead of requiring database bindings.

## Verification

The basic example verifies actual Astro output from a file and an HTTP source. `bun run test:site-build` also checks inline input, fixed revision and image SHA-256 verification. Hash mismatches, unavailable inputs and inconsistent revisions fail the build instead of selecting a different publication.

Private templates consume this public API through normal package dependencies. Deployment receipts and host admission remain host responsibilities; switching package names alone does not deploy or republish an existing site.

## Troubleshooting / Common Pitfalls

- A site ID or revision mismatch means the endpoint is not serving the expected publication; fix the source selection.
- Images need valid hashes and stable bytes. Do not disable verification to hide a failed fetch.
- CMS credentials belong only to the CMS request. They are not forwarded to external image URLs.
- Keep existing applications on their accepted package version until their own regression and deployment acceptance are complete.

---

Canonical guide: https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/guides/release/
Source: `docs/guides/release.md`

# Verify and Release SiteKit Packages

## Prerequisites

Use Node.js 24+, npm and Bun 1.4.0, public npm access, and a reviewed source revision. The private workspace root is never published. Targets are `@alneas/sitekit` and `@alneas/sitekit-cloudflare`; inspect their manifests for exact versions and dependency constraints.

Follow the [release policy](https://tech-docs.alneas.com/policies/release-policy.md) and [preparing-releases skill](https://tech-docs.alneas.com/skills/preparing-releases/SKILL.md). Preparation does not authorize commit, push, tag, registry or documentation deployment writes. Maintainers use the repository's `RELEASING.md` for local publication and recovery procedures.

## Public import

Install candidate archives using the [source verification guide](https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/guides/verify-source/). A minimal core import is:

```typescript
import { defineSite } from '@alneas/sitekit/config';
console.log(defineSite({ id: 'example', content: { snapshot: { siteId: 'example', revision: 1, posts: [], assets: [] } } }).id);
```

## Step-by-Step Implementation

### Review release impact and notes

Check pending Changesets with `bun run changeset status`. Select targets against an explicit baseline and confirm dependency delivery; do not infer publication from a local version heading. Maintainers explicitly prepare versions and cumulative package changelogs before the authorized release commit. Read the repository's `RELEASING.md` for the maintained commands and side effects.

```bash
bun run release:notes
```

This validates the current package/version notes without changing versions or consuming fragments. The release bundle includes package-specific `*.notes.md` and binds their SHA-256 hashes with the exact tested archives. The same entry supplies a separately authorized GitHub Release body. Registry publication, GitHub Release creation and documentation deployment are separate operations.


### 1. Verify the selected changes

```bash
bun install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org
bun run release:check
```

The gate checks Appkit registry versions and lockfile integrity, boundaries, public-file rules, types, documentation freshness, tests, static builds, Bun/npm packed consumers and the example build. Both consumer lanes inspect actual archives, exports, declarations, licenses and excluded files. Two exported CSS source files are intentional package assets. The Astro peer floor `>=7.3.3 <8` records the lowest version exercised by these checks.

Review affected targets and dependency delivery against their applicable release baseline. Record version choices and deliberate no-release decisions in the existing review process. Preserve existing release tags. Neither source version strings nor a GitHub release establish npm registration status.

### 2. Prepare a commit-bound release bundle

Complete source and generated-document changes before the authorized release commit. From clean, committed source:

```bash
bun run release:prepare
```

Preparation runs the full gate, packs npm archives and checks those exact archives in isolated Bun and npm consumers. The default destination is `.verification/releases/<commit>/`; `release.json` records commit, versions, archive hashes and toolchain identity. Use `--output-dir <path>` for a different destination. Keep local receipts outside public documentation and package payloads.

### 3. Validate the handoff

```bash
bun run release:verify --bundle .verification/releases/<commit>
```

This validates bundle/source identity without rebuilding. A changed source, version, dependency, packed file or amended commit requires a new bundle. Publish only the verified archive bytes after validation; do not rebuild or publish package directories in the publishing stage.

### 4. Use the required publication path

Subsequent versions require GitHub Actions with npm Trusted Publishing (OIDC), using the repository's `publish.yml` workflow. The account must trust the exact repository, workflow and environment when used, with permission for both publication and distribution-tag operations. Repository edits alone do not establish account configuration; unresolved trust setup blocks subsequent releases.

A genuinely new npm package's first registration alone may use an authorized manual session with the same commit-bound archives. Confirm that each package is new rather than inaccessible. A new workflow or a failed OIDC setup does not permit manual fallback for existing packages.

Publish core before the adapter when its dependency requires it, and confirm registry integrity before the dependent write. Below `1.0.0`, both `beta` and `latest` must point to the verified version. Confirm integrity and required tag mappings after publication; check for newer channels before tag writes. At or above `1.0.0`, require `latest` without changing `beta` under this rule.

### 0.2.0 dependency order

| Order | Package | Prepared version | Adoption requirement |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `@alneas/sitekit` | `0.2.0` | Complete staged publication and verify exact registry bytes. |
| 2 | `@alneas/sitekit-cloudflare` | `0.2.0` | Core `0.2.0` must already be readable; the adapter requires Core `^0.2.0`. |
| 3 | Consuming applications | Owner-selected | Pin both public packages exactly to `0.2.0` after delivery verification. |

The new management, connection and standalone APIs require this release pair.
The published `0.1.0` packages cannot substitute for it. A standalone host needs
no private SiteKit package. A managed host must additionally verify its own
execution API and authorization integration before activation.

For these existing packages, publish the Core GitHub Release
`sitekit-core-v0.2.0` first. Complete its original staging run and confirm
registry integrity and `beta`/`latest` before publishing
`sitekit-cloudflare-v0.2.0`. Publishing either Release triggers registry staging;
local preparation never performs that action. Follow `RELEASING.md` for approval,
completion and recovery. A registry-only consumer install is the adoption gate;
a local archive or source checkout is preparation evidence only.

### 5. Select documentation for the delivered targets

The `0.1.0` core and Cloudflare packages are published; the prepared `0.2.0` packages remain source candidates until registry verification succeeds. Keep their new APIs and usage out of the default released portal until registry publication is confirmed. A merged change, source tag, GitHub Release or locally generated guide is not proof of delivery.

After each target succeeds, select its reviewed source revision against the confirmed registry version. If only core is delivered, defer Cloudflare-only guides and API updates; do not advance the whole manifest merely because one target succeeded. If the portal cannot separate those revisions, defer the affected ingestion. Use a separate, clearly labeled development area only when the portal supports it.

For reviewed spelling, explanation or link corrections to already released behavior, a later documentation source revision is permitted without republishing the package. Keep generated API input at the released revision, or defer it when the newer source would expose unrelated candidate contracts. An immutable npm README or bundled guide changes only through a separately reviewed new package version.

Hand off only the approved public manifest documents and matching API entrypoints. Ingestion, portal-owned Japanese translation and portal deployment require their own authorization and checks. Local documentation preparation does not initiate any of those operations.

## Verification

A prepared bundle establishes local source/artifact identity and completed checks. Release completion additionally requires confirmed public versions, matching registry integrity, dependency resolution, required tags and a fresh registry-only consumer install. Verify delivered README/metadata after authorized publication. Report preparation, publication and remote verification separately; local success cannot prove account-side trust or remote delivery.

## Troubleshooting / Common Pitfalls

- Registry dependency or integrity mismatch: resolve the registry/lockfile conflict before release.
- Dirty source or bundle hash/commit mismatch: finish the reviewed source commit and prepare a new bundle; do not edit the manifest to bless changed bytes.
- Unresolved local dependency protocols in an archive: fix packaging and rerun both consumer lanes.
- Missing Trusted Publisher configuration or permissions: repair Actions/account setup before subsequent publication; do not introduce a manual fallback.
- Timeout or ambiguous registry response: stop writes, inspect version/integrity/tag state read-only, and resume only missing work. Never republish an existing version, delete successful targets or roll a newer channel backwards.
- Missing tags after successful publication: verify existing integrity and repair only missing required mappings; the release remains incomplete until confirmed.
- Generated-document drift: edit canonical sources, run `bun run docs:prepare`, then rerun checks. Keep operator receipts outside approved public content.

### 0.2.0 Appkit and documentation adoption

The unreleased 0.2.0 entries include optional Appkit Core 0.2.1 and React 0.3.0.
The optional React peer now requires ^0.3.0; update that consumer dependency with
SiteKit. React 0.3.0 itself declares Core 0.2.0 exactly, so a nested copy can remain
without overriding upstream metadata. Both installed versions are verified.
English and Japanese GitHub READMEs are paired; generated package README copies
are checked for freshness. Portal ingestion still follows confirmed delivery.
