Canonical guide: https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/guides/ai-consumer/
Source: `docs/guides/ai-consumer.md`

# Use SiteKit with a Coding Agent

## Prerequisites

Use the core package in an Astro site with Node.js 24 or later. Framework registry publication is pending; install the verified local artifact as shown in the [source guide](https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/guides/verify-source/). The bundled skill supports consuming sites and does not authorize package publication or deployment.

## Public import

Configure a site through `@alneas/sitekit/config`; ordinary configuration needs no React runtime, provider or CSS:

```typescript
import { defineSite } from '@alneas/sitekit/config';
const site = defineSite({ id: 'example', content: { snapshot: { siteId: 'example', revision: 1, posts: [], assets: [] } } });
console.log(site.id);
```

## Step-by-Step Implementation

### 1. Load the consumer guidance

Ask the agent to read `node_modules/@alneas/sitekit/skills/sitekit/SKILL.md`, adjusting the path for the package manager's installation layout. This is a packaged instruction file, not a JavaScript import or an automatically registered agent skill. Follow the agent client's documented installation mechanism when installing it as a named skill. The repository's `AGENTS.md` is for maintainers and is not shipped as consumer guidance.

### 2. Choose the documentation depth

Use `llms.txt` inside the package as an absolute-URL roadmap to the public portal. The packaged `llms-full.txt` concatenates the approved public guides in manifest order, with canonical source paths and public URLs. It is generated from those guides; source JSDoc remains the API behavior authority. These package files do not imply that the portal currently serves them at the same paths. Match guidance to the installed version or verified candidate: the default portal follows successfully delivered package versions and can lag unpublished source. If revisions differ, use the packaged guides and exported declarations rather than assuming a portal example is supported by the installed artifact.

### 3. Give the agent the relevant task

For configuration work, provide the chosen snapshot source and expected site/revision, using the [content-source guide](https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/guides/content-sources/). For basic editing, provide the host's authentication and provider constraints using the [Studio guide](https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/guides/public-studio/). Do not provide production credentials or customer records as example inputs. Optional external CMS integration and separately distributed extensions are defined in [architecture](https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/architecture/).

## Verification

The package contains `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt` and `skills/sitekit/SKILL.md`. The repository documentation gate verifies generated-guide freshness and typechecks the consumer skill's example alongside public guide/JSDoc examples. Bun and npm artifact checks verify that those files are actually present. Run the consuming site's normal typecheck/build and relevant behavior checks after applying agent changes.

## Troubleshooting / Common Pitfalls

- Missing guidance files: inspect the installed version and selected artifact; do not load files from a restricted sibling repository.
- Missing registry version: use the verified candidate archive or wait for the announced release; an example import does not establish npm availability.
- Relative web links: use the absolute URLs in `llms.txt`; packaged documentation is also readable offline.
- Agent proposes disabling authentication or integrity checks: repair the host configuration or content source instead. A successful import does not establish secure persistence or a production deployment.

---

Canonical guide: https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/errors/
Source: `docs/errors.md`

# SiteKit Error Codes

## Public import

Use `SiteKitError` and `SiteKitErrorCode` from `@alneas/sitekit/errors`. The class also appears in the root export. It requires no React provider or CSS. Content-file and build APIs remain Node-only; the error class itself performs no I/O.

## [CLASS] SiteKitError

Carries a stable code, corrective hint and public documentation link while remaining an ordinary `Error`.

### Signature

```typescript
import type { SiteKitErrorCode } from '@alneas/sitekit/errors';
declare class SiteKitError extends Error {
  readonly name: "SiteKitError";
  readonly code: SiteKitErrorCode;
  readonly hint: string;
  readonly docs: string;
  constructor(code: SiteKitErrorCode, message: string, options?: ErrorOptions);
}
```

### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| code | SiteKitErrorCode | Yes | One of the identifiers below; selects its hint and documentation anchor. |
| message | string | Yes | Failure context without credentials or sensitive payloads. |
| options.cause | unknown | No | Underlying failure, retained using standard Error cause semantics. |

### Result

Construction creates an Error whose `name` is `SiteKitError`. Its `message` includes `[code]`, context, hint and the `docs` URL. Match `code`, not message wording. `cause` may contain transport details or local paths; do not return it verbatim to browser clients or public logs. The class does not retry or authorize operations.

### Example

```typescript
import { defineSite } from '@alneas/sitekit/config';
import { SiteKitError } from '@alneas/sitekit/errors';
try {
  defineSite({ id: '', content: { file: './snapshot.json' } });
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof SiteKitError) console.error(error.code, error.hint, error.docs);
  else throw error;
}
```

## Codes and corrective actions

### SK_CONFIG_INVALID

A configuration has an empty/invalid ID, ambiguous content sources, unsupported endpoint/method or invalid revision. Supply one content source and a positive safe integer revision when present. Use credential-free HTTPS, or loopback HTTP for local development. The snapshot reader also rejects endpoint query strings and fragments. See [configuration](https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/api/).

### SK_CONTENT_MISSING

The build did not obtain a publication. Configure an inline snapshot, file or endpoint. Do not silently substitute another publication. An unconfigured standalone snapshot reader still returns `null`; the build requires content.

### SK_CONTENT_READ_FAILED

The snapshot file cannot be read, or an HTTP request/body read fails, times out, redirects or returns a non-success status. Check the source and build-only credentials. Native I/O/transport failures remain available as `cause` when present. A failed reader keeps the rejected promise and does not refetch a newer publication automatically; create a new reader for an intentional retry.

### SK_SNAPSHOT_INVALID

Serialization, JSON syntax, publication validation, the 8 MiB serialized limit or local draft-preview requirements fail. Correct the publication payload; `cause` retains parse/validation errors when present. Draft previews require explicit local-file preview mode and an unexpired draft marker. Do not disable validation or authorize previews from arbitrary HTTP inputs.

### SK_SITE_ID_MISMATCH

The publication belongs to a different site. Select the intended source. Do not bypass the identity check to render foreign content.

### SK_REVISION_MISMATCH

The publication revision differs from the configured expected revision. Select that pinned publication, or intentionally update the expected revision as part of a reviewed content change. This is not a request to retry until a different revision passes.

### SK_IMAGE_INVALID

Image metadata contains an unsafe/malformed URL, unsupported MIME type or conflicting hashes for one URL. Correct the publication metadata. Malformed snapshot hash fields may instead fail earlier with `SK_SNAPSHOT_INVALID`.

### SK_IMAGE_HASH_MISSING

A verified build requires missing image hashes. Publish SHA-256 hashes with the publication. Legacy compatibility remains explicit and does not bypass supplied hashes or a publication declaring SHA-256 integrity.

### SK_IMAGE_HASH_MISMATCH

Downloaded bytes do not match the publication's hash. Fix the bytes and hash together, then build that intended revision. Do not disable integrity checks.

### SK_IMAGE_FETCH_FAILED

An image request or streamed body fails, redirects, times out, returns a non-success status or has no body. Check image availability and host access. CMS authentication headers are not forwarded to media origins.

### SK_IMAGE_TOO_LARGE

An image declares or streams more than 25 MiB. Resize/re-encode the source and republish matching hashes.

## Coverage and compatibility

These codes cover failures owned by `defineSite`, the snapshot reader used by `createSiteAstroConfig`, and its image-verification step. Direct DTO parsers, storage adapters, Studio HTTP responses and Astro's own failures are outside this initial code set. Host source/configuration callbacks propagate their original errors unchanged; not every failure is a `SiteKitError`. Existing `instanceof Error` handling and diagnostic message substrings remain useful, but exact message text is not a stable API.

Use the [JSON Schema guide](https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/guides/site-schema/) for editor-time shape checking and the [content-source guide](https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/guides/content-sources/) for runtime source selection.

---

Canonical guide: https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/guides/site-schema/
Source: `docs/guides/site-schema.md`

# Validate Site Configuration with JSON Schema

## Prerequisites

Use the core package and Node.js 24 or later. Initial registry publication is pending; obtain the verified artifact using the [source guide](https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/guides/verify-source/). JSON Schema is an optional editor/validator aid; the runtime continues to validate settings with `defineSite`.

## Public import

The schema is a data export at `@alneas/sitekit/schema.json`, generated from the same Zod definition used by `@alneas/sitekit/config`. It requires no React runtime, provider or CSS. Schema generation uses repository tooling; consumers do not need Bun or Zod to read the JSON file.

## Step-by-Step Implementation

### 1. Associate a JSON configuration file in your editor

For an editor supporting VS Code's JSON settings, add this association to `.vscode/settings.json`:

```json
{
  "json.schemas": [
    {
      "fileMatch": ["site.config.json"],
      "url": "./node_modules/@alneas/sitekit/schema/site.schema.json"
    }
  ]
}
```

Adjust the file location for your package manager. Do not add a `$schema` property to the site configuration itself: the runtime configuration is strict and does not accept extra fields.

### 2. Describe exactly one content source

Save as `site.config.json`:

```json
{
  "id": "example",
  "revision": 1,
  "content": { "file": "./snapshot.json" }
}
```

Use exactly one `snapshot`, `file` or `endpoint` property under `content`. The file branch alone permits `draftPreview`; the endpoint branch alone permits `method: "GET" | "POST"`.

### 3. Keep runtime validation authoritative

In an Astro configuration, use the public runtime entry point as usual:

```typescript
import { defineSite } from '@alneas/sitekit/config';
const site = defineSite({ id: 'example', revision: 1, content: { file: './snapshot.json' } });
console.log(site.id);
```

The JSON Schema uses draft 2020-12 and Zod's **input** shape. It describes required fields, mutually exclusive source branches, positive safe-integer revisions, URI format and rejection of extra properties. Configure your validator's URI-format support; not every JSON Schema implementation enforces formats by default.

JSON Schema does not execute Zod's custom refinements or normalize strings. A whitespace-only ID/file or a URI containing credentials or an unsupported scheme can pass shape validation and still fail `defineSite`. The snapshot reader additionally checks publication contents, site identity/revision, query/fragment restrictions and draft-preview permission. Inline `snapshot` is intentionally unconstrained in this configuration schema and is validated only when read. Passing the schema is not proof of authorization, integrity or build success.

## Verification

After installing the package, verify the exported data with Node:

```bash
node --input-type=module -e 'import schema from "@alneas/sitekit/schema.json" with { type: "json" }; console.log(schema.title)'
```

Expected output: `SiteKit site configuration`. The repository's tests exercise the generated schema using an independent draft-2020-12 validator, compare accepted/rejected shapes with runtime validation and explicitly test the documented refinement differences. `docs:generated` regenerates the schema into temporary storage and fails on drift; `docs:prepare` explicitly refreshes normal generated output.

## Troubleshooting / Common Pitfalls

- Missing schema export: inspect the installed artifact/version and its `exports`; do not point an editor at a sibling source checkout.
- Both `file` and `endpoint`: choose one source; no fallback selection is implied.
- Schema passes but the build fails: apply runtime URL, publication, access and image-integrity checks. Consult the [error code reference](https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/errors/).
- Modified generated schema: update the canonical Zod definition and generator, regenerate explicitly, then rerun tests and freshness checks. Do not repair the generated JSON by hand.

---

Canonical guide: https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/guides/workflow-supply/
Source: `docs/workflow-supply.md`

# Maintain workflow supply and local quality

## Prerequisites

Use the Node runtimes and pinned Bun declared in `.github/workflow-adapter.json`, the committed lockfile and the project's existing secret-scanner setup. No private checkout or private package credentials are needed. The installed supply is a reviewed local bundle, including uncommitted upstream changes; it has not been published by this adoption.

## Public import

This guide uses repository commands such as `bun run workflow:check`; it does not require a runtime package import.

## Step-by-Step Implementation

Run `bun run quality:commit` against staged changes. It scans staged secrets and lints index bytes without changing files or staging. Run `bun run quality:push` before pushing. Existing hooks are preserved; this adoption does not install or enable hooks. Inspect `git config --get core.hooksPath` and the repository's hook files when checking local activation. CI independently enforces the verification contract.

Edit `.github/workflow-adapter.json` or `scripts/workflow-project/roles.json`, then run `bun run workflow:generate` explicitly. Never hand-edit generated workflows or the installed shared bundle. Update the supply only from reviewed source with its recorded base revision and exact local bundle digest. `workflow:check` detects drift without fixing it.

### Shared workflow contract

| Role | Adoption and owner |
| --- | --- |
| Source quality | Required: main push, PR and manual; `ci.yml` calls reusable quality. |
| Shared package quality | Required: callable only, preserving the declared runtime matrix. |
| Publish npm packages | Required: stable published Release stages verified archives; manual dispatch completes an original staging run. |
| Complete approved npm release | Required for subsequent staged releases: observe approval using default-branch code and request completion. |
| Documentation freshness | Verification is owned by source quality; no second full source gate. |
| UI browser tests | Existing relevant project checks remain owned by source quality; no duplicate standalone workflow. |
| Auth integration tests | No independent auth workflow adopted; existing applicable integration checks remain in the project gate. |
| Record npm deployments | Not adopted: no existing standalone retrospective deployment-record command; publication completion owns its existing records. |

Common code owns naming, standard triggers, scoped credentials, main-only successful task-cache writes, evidence and deterministic generation. Project fragments own commands, service/browser prerequisites, target/tag rules, supported runtime coverage, archive contents and size budgets. Steps are labeled `Shared:` or `Project:`. The public extension is additive beside the existing private supply; the private implementation is unchanged.

### Project-specific verification

The shared selector narrows standalone Markdown guide changes and publication-only helper changes; publication helpers run their gate/tooling checks without unrelated package/browser suites. Runtime, packaged README, dependency, export and unknown changes retain the broad existing gate. Fine package/browser selection remains conservative; adoption does not establish that finer optimization.

The mandatory secret-history check still runs. Selection requires a latest successful main run/attempt, successful jobs for every declared Node runtime and an unexpired immutable receipt with compatible execution identity. Failed intervening changes stay in scope. Missing/incompatible evidence, history or API access select full verification. Executed checks, exact-input local reuse and out-of-scope omissions are different outcomes. Local/PR success cannot satisfy a Release's official source-evidence requirement.

Release verification requires Source quality success for the exact selected commit and keeps existing current-archive and registry checks. Release preparation reuses deterministic source suites only after validating the exact official main proof; it retains the real build and current archive/registry checks. Staging and completion retain the existing npm implementation, original run/attempt/artifact binding and manual bootstrap. No build or direct npm publish runs in registry-writing jobs. Human npm approval is separate; pending staging is not release success.

## Verification

Run `bun run conformance:check` for project wiring and `bun run conformance:verify` for the shared regressions plus this project's maintained gate/publication/cache probes. `workflow:check` remains the read-only generated-output checker. Expected: generated output is unchanged and supplier regression tests pass. Project source and release tooling checks remain mandatory where applicable. A changed or deleted generated workflow must make `workflow:check` fail without repair; regenerate only after reviewing the source change.

Local fixture coverage and generated YAML do not prove execution on GitHub. Before an authorized rollout, review required-check names and npm Trusted Publisher/environment bindings for workflow renames. Preserve any pending original staging runs and their recovery contract. This work does not authorize a push, publication or deployment.

## Troubleshooting / Common Pitfalls

If no trusted baseline is available, full verification is expected. If Release source evidence is absent or incompatible, run the exact commit through main Source quality before staging; never substitute a PR run or local log. If generated output drifts, inspect canonical adapter/fragments and explicitly regenerate. If npm approval finishes after the observer deadline, complete with the original staging run; never rebuild or restage to finish approval.

Release impact: no package version bump; this change owns maintainer workflow tooling and verification only.

Conformance has three independent levels: shared implementation regressions, installed project wiring, and local behavioral probes. GitHub event execution remains unverified until an authorized remote run. Mandatory outcomes are catalogued centrally in the supplied `requirements.json`; hook-manager choice is a recommendation. The central supply owns adoption status and exception review; local guides describe only this project's implementation.

Conformance probes are selected from changed governance inputs, not run in full for every change. Use `bun run conformance:verify --base <reviewed-ref>` for an explicit committed range. The report distinguishes executed probes, exact-input reused probes and out-of-scope probes. Existing Turbo tasks keep their own actual success cache; this adoption adds no new task orchestrator.

## Package selection

Normal source verification reads a fingerprint-bound plan from the shared selector. Package source and test changes select the owning workspace and all reverse-transitive consumers, including runtime, peer, optional, development and literal cross-workspace source dependencies. Manifest, export, dependency, lockfile, build configuration and unknown shared changes retain full coverage. A changed workspace inventory fails closed until its adapter is updated. Missing or incompatible successful evidence also selects full coverage.

The plan records selected and omitted package tests separately from cache hits. It is checked against the current source fingerprint, commit and actual execution environment before execution. Local snapshots never establish official main or Release success.

SiteKit keeps its original release-check gate list, replacing only package test/typecheck invocations with explicit affected Turbo filters. Turbo retains upstream builds and actual-runtime cache identity. Node 26 uses the same selected test/typecheck coverage and restores required builds even for an unchanged selection. The paired archive, site-build, npm/Bun consumer and example gates remain coupled and run under their existing contracts. Explicit `quality:full` and Release commands remain full.

## Development policy inventory

The pinned `development-requirements.json` maps every clause of the reviewed shared development policy. It is descriptive evidence mapping, not a project policy profile or permission to omit a mandatory gate. `conformance:check` inspects active dependency groups, literal imports, TypeScript aliases, ignored evidence paths and declared documentation/artifact inputs. Computed module resolution and untested UI, database, authorization and human-review contracts remain explicitly unverified.

Run `bun run conformance:audit` for the complete clause inventory, existing test candidates, current source/environment identity and read-only hook status. Add `--probe-commit` to exercise the actual commit command in disposable repositories: clean and invalid index contents, a synthetic secret, missing scanner configuration and missing scanner binary. The probe preserves working files and index bytes and does not activate hooks. Existing secret/history scans remain fresh outside deterministic task caches.

The shared commit gate scans staged bytes and lints an isolated index snapshot. Hook files call the maintained commands; having hook files does not establish local activation. Inspect the audit result before claiming hooks run automatically. The source workflow performs dependency-free supply preflight, then critical inspection through its maintained selector after dependency restoration. Required failures stop the gate; inventory entries without behavioral proof are never reported as a full policy pass.

Conformance verification selects bounded tooling/commit probes for relevant verifier, hook or configuration changes. Ordinary prose and unrelated package changes do not select browser or database suites. Actual archive inspection is available with `node scripts/workflow-supply/public/policy-critical.mjs --archive <archive.tgz>`; it checks member paths/types and identity, and does not replace the existing isolated consumers, license/notices, scanner or fresh registry checks.

### Bounded GitHub policy diagnostics

Manually dispatch `ci.yml` on the reviewed branch with `verification_mode=conformance` to exercise shared/owning selector regressions and the actual commit gate on Node 24 and 26. An identical second deterministic task must reuse success; ordinary prose selects no extra probes. Use `verification_mode=negative` separately to run a clean control and then stage a synthetic secret in disposable repositories. The required step must fail with `indexed-secret-blocked`, and the downstream success sentinel must be skipped. Diagnostic concurrency is isolated from normal source verification.

The default `full` mode and normal PR/main gates retain existing checks. Diagnostics do not run product/browser/DB suites, save remote task caches or issue authoritative source evidence. Their artifacts record scoped results, not full policy compliance. Before merging, satisfy the normal required PR checks independently.

## Reviewed supply update (2026-10-31)

The installed shared workflow bundle is selected from github-docs main revision
`86e098c937186277b9b18c8a0ac5f654a21c7116`. Its installer records exact
bundle/output hashes in `.github/workflow-supply.json`. Ready PR and merge-queue
triggers and authenticated successful-ancestor selection follow that reviewed
supply. Existing project verification commands and runtime coverage remain owned
by this project. Optional local publication and additional evidence adapters are
not enabled by copying the supplier. Run `workflow:check`, the owning workflow
regressions and conformance checks after updates. Local verification does not
establish GitHub execution, branch protection or registry publication.

# Run Standalone Marketing Measurement

## Prerequisites

Use the core and Cloudflare artifacts from the same verified source candidate, Node.js 24+ for build/tooling, and a host-provisioned D1 database. This feature has no managed CMS account or private SDK requirement. A static website still needs a server endpoint for persistence and confirmed outcomes. Generate your actual Worker binding types in the consuming host.

## Public import

Use `@alneas/sitekit/marketing` for the shared contract, strict validation and CSV spending parser. Use `@alneas/sitekit-cloudflare/marketing` for storage, schema, routes and optional integration signatures. Advanced management screens and social publishing are separate extensions; the measurement provider advertises `socialPublishing: false`.

## Step-by-Step Implementation

### 1. Apply the schema and configure the server

Apply `marketingSchemaSql` once through your host's explicit D1 migration tooling. The provider never creates tables implicitly. Configure collection coverage and verified scope on the server; do not take site/tenant selection from request JSON.

```typescript
import {
  createD1MarketingServices, createMarketingHandler,
  createHmacMarketingAuthorizer, marketingSchemaSql,
  type MarketingDatabase,
} from '@alneas/sitekit-cloudflare/marketing';

// This illustrates the required bindings; use generated binding types in your host.
interface MeasurementEnv {
  DB: MarketingDatabase;
  SITE_ID: string;
  COLLECTION_STARTED_AT: string;
  OUTCOME_SIGNING_SECRET: string;
  REPORT_SIGNING_SECRET: string;
}
const authorize = createHmacMarketingAuthorizer<MeasurementEnv>({
  keys: env => [
    { id: 'booking', secret: env.OUTCOME_SIGNING_SECRET,
      scope: { siteId: env.SITE_ID }, operations: ['outcome'], outcomeSource: 'booking' },
    { id: 'reporting', secret: env.REPORT_SIGNING_SECRET,
      scope: { siteId: env.SITE_ID }, operations: ['report', 'spend', 'forget', 'purge'] },
  ],
});
export const fetch = createMarketingHandler<MeasurementEnv>({
  publicScope: env => ({ siteId: env.SITE_ID }),
  services: (env, scope) => createD1MarketingServices({
    database: env.DB, scope, startedAt: env.COLLECTION_STARTED_AT, retentionDays: 90,
  }),
  authorize,
});
// Supply this SQL to your migration tooling; do not execute it on every request.
export const migration = marketingSchemaSql;
```

Store independent, random signing secrets in server secret bindings; use at least 32 bytes. Never put them in browser configuration. Schedule `services.analytics.purge()` to enforce retention, and configure rate controls on public ingestion. This example does not provision infrastructure or supply a user login/session implementation.

### 2. Collect events and return an attribution reference

Install `initBrowserAnalytics` from `@alneas/sitekit/analytics` with the site's configured ID and `/api/analytics`. Retain the consent policy and stylesheet from the analytics integration. `analytics.attributionReference()` returns an opaque reference only while consent is effective; pass it in an explicitly supported form or booking handoff and return it with a trusted outcome. Do not put it in general share links or assume an external booking provider preserves it.

No reference, withdrawn permission or an expired lookback produces an unattributed outcome. Browser collection refuses `conversion` and `booking_complete`. An outbound booking click is a booking start, not a confirmed reservation. The host can invoke the scoped `forget` operation when processing a privacy request; clearing browser storage alone does not delete previously stored records.

The store hashes references before persistence. Forgetting atomically clears existing links and stores a scoped hash revocation marker, so delayed events cannot restore them. Retention cleanup removes measurement records but retains these minimal revocation markers; retire them only as part of an explicit installation/data lifecycle policy. Long-lived browser tabs rotate expired references before emitting events or handing them to an integration.

### 3. Use protected integration routes

| Route | Method and input | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/api/analytics` | POST analytics batch; same-origin browser request | Consent/site/time-filtered durable event acknowledgement |
| `/api/marketing/outcomes` | POST trusted outcome JSON | Immutable source/event receipt |
| `/api/marketing/spend` | POST spending import JSON or `text/csv` | Atomic counts of inserted and duplicate rows |
| `/api/marketing/report` | GET `from`, `to`, `timezone`, `currency` | Site and campaign reports |
| `/api/marketing/forget` | POST `{ attributionId }` | Remove scoped attribution links |
| `/api/marketing/purge` | POST `{}` | Delete expired scoped records |

The protected routes require host authorization. The included HMAC authorizer verifies `X-SiteKit-Key-Id`, `X-SiteKit-Timestamp` (Unix seconds), and `X-SiteKit-Signature` (lowercase HMAC-SHA256 hex). Sign these six UTF-8 values joined by newline, with no trailing newline: `sitekit-marketing-v1`, key ID, timestamp, HTTP method, full request URL, and lowercase SHA-256 hex of the exact request body bytes. GET uses the hash of the empty body. Signatures expire after five minutes; immutable source/event or spending-row IDs suppress replay effects within that window. Provider secrets stay on the integration server. Rotate keys with distinct IDs and an explicit overlap period.

Example outcome: `{ "source": "booking", "eventId": "reservation-42", "kind": "booking", "occurredAt": "2026-10-20T00:00:00Z", "amountMinor": 15000, "currency": "JPY" }`. Add `attributionId` only if the integration returns the consent reference. A key authorized for `booking` cannot submit an outcome under `forms` or a different site.

CSV headings are exactly `id,occurredAt,source,medium,campaign,amountMinor,currency` (order may vary). Empty acquisition cells are omitted. IDs are stable across imports; reimporting the same row is safe, while changing its amount under the same ID conflicts. Allocate spending to the reporting interval using an explicit timestamp. For a correction, prepare a separately reviewed accounting adjustment workflow; silently replacing an immutable row is unsupported.

### 4. Interpret the report

The model is `last-non-direct-30d-v1`: choose the latest non-direct, consented acquisition record at or before the outcome, within an inclusive 30-day window and the same site/tenant/reference. Ties use stable event identity. Reports re-evaluate late-arriving records and expose `asOf`, `retainedFrom`, `lookbackComplete` and `spendCoverage: recorded-only`.

Amounts are integer currency minor units. CPA is recorded spending divided by confirmed leads plus bookings. ROAS uses confirmed attributed revenue divided by recorded spending. Null means unavailable; missing spending, unknown outcome values and mixed currencies are not converted to zero. Explicit zero spending permits a zero CPA when conversions exist, but ROAS remains unavailable. These are site-observed metrics, not a claim of advertising-platform impressions, billed spending or platform-attributed conversions. No conversion export or automatic ad-cost API synchronization is included.

Dates are explicit inclusive/exclusive instants; timezone is presentation metadata, not an implicit conversion of date-only strings. For an Asia/Tokyo calendar day, send the correct UTC/offset boundaries. Never sum across currencies without a separately defined exchange-rate policy.

## Verification

The storage tests use real SQLite statements, uniqueness constraints, transactional rollback and provider re-creation. Run `bun run test:all`, `bun run typecheck:all`, `bun run verify:public`, `bun run test:site-build` and `bun run test:consumer`. The packed-consumer check exercises the published subpaths from installed archives without private SDKs. Local SQLite/Node Web Crypto evidence does not establish deployed D1 or a live booking integration; run those acceptance checks against your provisioned host separately.

## Troubleshooting / Common Pitfalls

- **401/403:** verify signature age, exact URL/body, key operation/source policy and same-origin mutation policy. Cross-origin cookies are not a substitute for host authorization.
- **400/413/415:** correct strict DTO/CSV fields, content type and the 128 KiB request limit. Spending imports accept at most 100 rows.
- **409:** an existing source/event or spending identity has a different immutable payload. Do not retry with silently modified values.
- **422:** report bounds exceed retained coverage, 93 days or 10,000 period records, or trusted input lies outside collection/retention bounds. Narrow the period or choose a provider designed for a larger volume.
- **503:** storage, configuration or provider resolution is unavailable. Tables must be explicitly migrated; a missing managed provider never silently falls back to standalone.
- **Unattributed or null metrics:** inspect coverage, the handoff reference, timestamps and currencies. Lack of a confirmed outcome cannot be repaired by counting a browser click as a sale.

Canonical guide: https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/guides/connection-contracts/
Source: `docs/guides/connection-contracts.md`

# Connection and template contracts

`@alneas/sitekit/connection` supplies data-only connection metadata and portable
template descriptions. It does not connect an account, install a CMS, register a
template or authorize premium services. Every protected operation must check the
current authenticated actor, site and service entitlement on the server.

```ts
import { parseSiteConnection, parseSiteTemplateDescriptor } from '@alneas/sitekit/connection';
const off = { available: false, reason: 'not_configured' } as const;
const connection = parseSiteConnection({
  protocolVersion: 1, connectionId: 'c1', siteId: 'site1', status: 'disconnected',
  capabilities: { content: off, measurement: off, socialPublishing: off, multiSiteManagement: off },
});
const template = parseSiteTemplateDescriptor({
  protocolVersion: 1, id: 'basic', version: '1.0.0', locales: ['en'],
  collections: [{ id: 'pages', contentType: 'PAGE', schema: { type: 'object' },
    recordIdentity: { kind: 'localized-slug' }, mediaReferencePaths: [] }],
  mediaPolicy: { requiredAltLocales: [] },
});
```

Protocol version 1 rejects unknown versions, fields and capability names. Reasons
for unavailable capabilities are `subscription_required`, `not_configured`,
`forbidden` and `unavailable`. A disconnected or reauthorization-required connection
cannot advertise available operations. Capabilities are display hints, never access
tokens. No credentials or internal storage/plugin metadata belong in these objects.

`PublishedSiteSnapshot` aliases the existing `EaosCmsPublishedSnapshot` type. Use
`parsePublishedSnapshot` from `@alneas/sitekit/content` for its existing validation;
there is no new envelope, revision interpretation or snapshot hash algorithm.

Descriptors are limited to 256 KiB of UTF-8 JSON, 32 levels of JSON nesting,
32 collections and 16 locales. IDs/content types and locales must be unique;
collection and required-alt locales are subsets of the template locales. Runtime
functions, accessors, non-JSON objects, cycles, sparse arrays and prototype keys
are rejected. Template versions use SemVer and must be immutable in the host registry.
The parser returns detached data. It does not execute the schema.

The schema profile supports `type`, `properties`, `required`, `additionalProperties`,
`items`, `propertyNames`, `$defs`, local acyclic `$ref`, `oneOf`, `anyOf`, `allOf`,
`enum`, `const`, `default`, `title`, `description`, `pattern`, `format`, numeric bounds,
`multipleOf`, string/array/object length bounds and `uniqueItems`. Supported formats
are `date`, `date-time`, `uri`, `email`, `uuid`. Definitions and all referenced targets
must be schema objects. Remote references and unrecognized keywords are rejected.
Hosts still need a bounded schema evaluator to validate actual document values.

Explicit portable annotations are `x-ui` (string `label`, `group`, `width`,
`placeholder`, and a recognized `widget`) and boolean `x-date`. An `x-date` field
requires valid calendar-date semantics: interpret the value as a date and require
the UTC calendar date to match its first ten characters. A host interpreter must
implement this in addition to ordinary schema validation. Private database or
code-generation annotations are not accepted. Explicit `mediaReferencePaths`
replace implicit media annotations; ordinary string fields are never relationships.
A relationship path is an array of segments; `*` iterates an array. Optional `when`
conditions compare a document-relative path against a JSON scalar. All conditions
must match; wildcard conditions refer to the same array element as the path.

Record identity recipes are `locale`, `slug`, `localized-slug` (locale/slug), or
`localized-data` with a field path and `fallback: 'slug'`. These are declarations for
an authorized host to interpret, not executable callbacks. Optional collection
metadata includes label, locales, rich-text/media support and body requirement.
The descriptor must be registered by a trusted host, never taken from an arbitrary
browser request as authority. Subscription and authorization enforcement belong to
the service receiving operations, regardless of source-code visibility.

Canonical guide: https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/guides/management-settings/
Source: `docs/guides/management-settings.md`

# Shared management settings

`@alneas/sitekit/management` provides React-free public contracts and one settings
policy for standalone and EAOS-connected hosts. It does not mount a screen,
provision authentication/storage, implement an EAOS execution API, run an external
application effect, or switch execution ownership.

## Data and defaults

`SettingsValues` groups site identity, localization/timezone, measurement,
reporting currency and automatic social publication rules. Bootstrap requires the
site identity, locale routing/timezone and currency. Only new-install measurement
and social fields have defaults: measurement disabled, 90 days' retention,
opt-in consent with a 180-day choice lifetime, automatic publication disabled and
approval required. Consent mode uses the existing browser collector vocabulary;
settings do not manufacture a visitor's analytics consent.

Existing hosts must import their actual saved/effective state and verified receipts;
never initialize defaults over an existing installation. An origin is HTTPS without
credentials, query or fragment. Locale IDs are canonicalized and unique, the
default locale must belong to them, and timezone/currency must be runtime-supported.
Saved commands require the complete selected section, so omitted fields cannot
silently reset an existing value. A timezone change never reschedules existing
UTC jobs, and a currency change never converts historical money.

```typescript
import { parseSettingsValues, createSettingsRecord } from '@alneas/sitekit/management';
const values = parseSettingsValues({
  site: { name: 'Example', url: 'https://example.com' },
  localization: { defaultLocale: 'en', locales: ['en'], prefixStrategy: 'never', timezone: 'UTC' },
  reporting: { currency: 'USD' },
});
const initial = createSettingsRecord({
  scope: { tenantId: 'tenant', siteId: 'site' },
  authority: { kind: 'standalone', epoch: 'generation-1', status: 'active' },
  values,
});
// The trusted host atomically creates initial only when that scoped record is absent.
export { initial };
```

## Save, apply and completion

`ManagementSettingsProvider` defines context, settings, save, apply and application
status. Marketing/social screen operations can compose with this surface. Existing
marketing screens are not migrated by this entry alone.

Every command has `protocolVersion: 1`, a stable `commandId`, the reviewed aggregate
`expectedVersion` and `authorityEpoch`. Scope and actor are resolved by the server,
not accepted from command JSON. `saveSettings` stores a draft and returns a durable
receipt without changing runtime state. `applySettings` additionally names the
exact `savedRevision` and `expectedEffectiveRevision` (null before first application).
It reserves an application and captures that value; it never calls a build or SNS.

Each section has saved/effective revisions and its latest application. Use
`settingsSectionStatus` for `not_applied`, `applying`, `applied` or `failed` relative
to the current saved draft. Inspect the application separately when an older
revision is still applying. Another same-section application is rejected while
one is pending; other sections can progress independently. A newer draft can be
saved while an older revision applies, and confirmation preserves that newer draft.

Trusted hosts execute reserved requests through their existing application path,
using the captured value in `SettingsRecord.applications`. Completion is server-only:
`completeApplication` is deliberately absent from the browser provider. Its separate
permission and `verifyApplication` port must confirm a receipt bound to the scope,
application, captured value, revision and authority epoch. A generic receipt ID is
not evidence by itself. Application is effective only after a verified receipt;
uncertain outcomes remain pending. A failed outcome requires proof the rejected
operation cannot apply later; a transport timeout is not such proof.

```typescript
import { createManagementSettingsService, type ManagementSettingsServiceOptions } from '@alneas/sitekit/management';
export async function saveAndRequestApply(options: ManagementSettingsServiceOptions) {
  const service = createManagementSettingsService(options);
  const snapshot = await service.settings();
  await service.saveSettings({
    protocolVersion: 1, commandId: crypto.randomUUID(),
    expectedVersion: snapshot.version, authorityEpoch: snapshot.authority.epoch,
    section: 'site', value: { ...snapshot.sections.site.saved.value, name: 'Updated' },
  });
  const saved = await service.settings();
  return service.applySettings({
    protocolVersion: 1, commandId: crypto.randomUUID(),
    expectedVersion: saved.version, authorityEpoch: saved.authority.epoch,
    section: 'site', savedRevision: saved.sections.site.saved.revision,
    expectedEffectiveRevision: saved.sections.site.effective?.revision ?? null,
  });
}
```

## Host admission and persistence

`createManagementSettingsService` requires a bound authenticated scope, durable
`ManagementSettingsStore`, live `authorize` callback and existing-receipt verifier.
There is no allow-all default. The host resolves the actor outside browser input.
Authorization receives the selected section/proposed value for destination-level
checks and returns `SettingsAdmission`: the current decision plus an opaque
permission generation. It runs before reading and again before committing or
returning replay information. The authorizer and store must bind the same verified
actor/site and advance that generation for relevant role, destination, capability
or subscription changes. The completion privilege must be separate from ordinary apply access.
Display capabilities/permissions from `ManagementContext` never grant server access.

`compareAndSwap` must atomically match tenant, site, aggregate version and authority
epoch **and the current permission generation** (`expectedPermissionVersion`),
returning literal false without changing any row on conflict. Literal true is the
only success acknowledgement; malformed/truthy responses fail unavailable. The service performs
no automatic write retry or merge. Changing an authority status/epoch must change
its aggregate version too; the host must prevent an old generation from recreating
or overwriting the record. Bootstrap is an atomic create, never a CAS upsert.
Both backends must meet these persistence invariants even if their DB APIs differ.
A separate authorization check followed by an unguarded DB write is insufficient.
Use an atomic admission/version comparison or the host's transactional grant/permit
primitive when permissions are not stored alongside the settings; do not mirror
an eventually consistent permission flag and claim equivalent revocation safety.

Paused/transferring owners reject new save/apply requests. Trusted completion of an
already admitted effect may still record verified facts while paused, under the
same epoch and fresh completion authorization; it does not start another effect.
An epoch change rejects the old completion. Distributed execution permits and
connect/disconnect transfer are later host work; this CAS fence alone is not a
complete cross-service or external-side-effect fencing protocol.

The service keeps command receipts and application history in the same atomic
aggregate. Identical command replays return their existing result after fresh
permission checks, including after process restart. A changed payload, operation
kind or authority epoch under an old ID is a conflict. A save replay returns its
original acknowledgement/version; reload settings for current state. Apply replay
returns the application's current status. Never overwrite local unsaved input on
409: reload/review the current revision and issue a deliberate new command.

This initial record is bounded to 256 command receipts, 128 applications and
1 MiB of serialized UTF-8 JSON. New commands fail at capacity; no dedupe/history
entries are silently evicted. A production host must plan explicit archival and
retain replay tombstones before reaching these limits. Scope-mismatched or malformed
records fail closed. Internal storage/provider exceptions become safe unavailable
faults, not browser diagnostics. Host HTTP mappings are invalid=400, forbidden=403,
conflict=409, unavailable=503 and capacity=413.

The conformance corpus uses real local in-memory SQLite, an atomically fenced
permission-generation table and two execution-owner profiles. It recreates service
objects to prove receipts belong to the store rather than a service-instance cache;
it does not reopen the database or restart a process.
It proves shared contract policy and durable CAS behavior, not a deployed EAOS
adapter, native entitlement service or an external application's successful effect.
