Canonical guide: https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/guides/management-console/
Source: `docs/guides/management-console.md`

# Embed the Shared Management Console

## Prerequisites

Use the public Core and Cloudflare packages from the same release, React 19 and a
verified administrator session. Provision D1 with `managementSchemaSql` once.
An existing host supplies its canonical report, encrypted Meta connection and
publication ports. No EAOS or private Appkit package is required by these screens
or adapters. This entry supplies reusable UI, HTTP and settings storage; it does
not provision login, Meta applications, deployment or a publication scheduler.

The settings policy and effect-proof requirements are defined in
[Shared Management Settings](https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/guides/management-settings/). Existing installations
import their actual values instead of resetting them to installation defaults.

## Public import

```tsx
import { ManagementApp, ManagementWorkspace } from '@alneas/sitekit/management/react';
import type { ManagementWorkspaceProps } from '@alneas/sitekit/management/react';
import '@alneas/sitekit/management/styles.css';

export function Standalone(props: ManagementWorkspaceProps) {
  return <ManagementApp {...props} />;
}
export function Embedded(props: ManagementWorkspaceProps) {
  return <section aria-label="Selected site"><ManagementWorkspace {...props} /></section>;
}
```

Both mounts render the same settings, advertising, post and account components.
`ManagementApp` adds SiteKit's sidebar; `ManagementWorkspace` supplies only the
workspace and common page navigation. Styles are scoped below
`.sitekit-management`; they do not style the enclosing host. No global `main`,
router, login screen or private design-system dependency is added.

## Step-by-Step Implementation

### 1. Bind a browser workspace

```typescript
import { createManagementHttpProvider } from '@alneas/sitekit/management/http';
import type { ManagementBinding } from '@alneas/sitekit/management/react';
import type { ManagementContext } from '@alneas/sitekit/management';

export function bind(context: ManagementContext, verifiedSessionGeneration: string): ManagementBinding {
  return {
    identityKey: verifiedSessionGeneration,
    context,
    provider: createManagementHttpProvider({ origin: 'https://example.test' }),
  };
}
```

Obtain context through the authenticated host, never construct granted rights from
browser form input. Change `identityKey` when the principal/session changes. A
site, execution owner or authority epoch change creates a fresh workspace. Scope
switches prompt for unsaved changes; identity changes clear the old workspace
immediately. Choosing to stay retains the accepted workspace; the host should keep
its site selection consistent. A subsequent new binding object can request the
same site again. Do not mutate a binding object in place.

Pass `initialQuery` with UTC `from`/`to`, IANA `timezone` and ISO `currency`. Effective
localization/report settings supply the initial defaults for the marketing screen.
Changing the timezone does not move scheduled UTC jobs. The host's account/job
ports remain authoritative; the UI never dispatches directly to Meta.

### 2. Connect the authenticated standalone server

```typescript
import { createManagementHandler, createD1ManagementSettingsStore } from '@alneas/sitekit-cloudflare/management';
import type { ManagementSession } from '@alneas/sitekit-cloudflare/management';
import type { CloudflareD1Database } from '@alneas/sitekit-cloudflare';
import { createManagementSettingsService } from '@alneas/sitekit/management';
import type { ManagementConsoleProvider, ManagementSettingsServiceOptions } from '@alneas/sitekit/management';

interface HostSession {
  subject: string;
  provider: ManagementConsoleProvider;
  policy: Omit<ManagementSettingsServiceOptions, 'store'>;
  authorize: ManagementSession['authorize'];
}
interface Bindings { db: CloudflareD1Database }

export function standaloneGateway(
  resolveVerifiedSession: (request: Request, env: Bindings) => Promise<HostSession | null>,
) {
  return createManagementHandler<Bindings>({
    origin: 'https://example.test',
    async session(request, env) {
      const verified = await resolveVerifiedSession(request, env);
      if (!verified) return null;
      const service = createManagementSettingsService({
        ...verified.policy,
        store: createD1ManagementSettingsStore(env.db, verified.subject),
      });
      return {
        scope: verified.policy.scope,
        authorize: verified.authorize,
        provider: {
          ...verified.provider,
          settings: { ...service, context: () => verified.provider.settings.context() },
        },
      };
    },
  });
}
```

The resolver verifies the actual login/session and site grant. It supplies fresh
capabilities, operation permissions and the actor-bound marketing services; a
caller-controlled identity header is insufficient. The policy's authorizer checks
live rights for each operation and returns a permission generation. Maintain the
matching `(tenant_id,site_id,subject,version,allowed)` row in
`sitekit_management_admission`. Every relevant role, destination, subscription or
capability change must atomically advance that generation with the authoritative
ACL change; a stale mirrored ACL in a different database does not satisfy this
contract. The single SQL compare-and-swap checks that live generation together
with settings version and authority epoch. There is no allow-all default.

Provision new records with `createSettingsRecord` and
`initializeD1ManagementSettings`; existing records are never overwritten. Keep the
server-side aggregate private. Runtime/public builds read only confirmed effective
sections; a draft is not a runtime policy. Reserve apply through the common service,
then let the trusted build/runtime port process the immutable captured application
value. Complete it only with a verified matching effect or definitive rejection
receipt. An uncertain outcome stays applying. Completion has no browser endpoint.

Use `sections.social.effective.value` as the publication hook's canonical rule.
Remove the old immediate `saveRule` form/route when adopting this workspace. Applying
it affects later successful content-publication events, not already queued posts.
Do not keep a second editable rule under the social store. The host's worker must
check live permission and authority before external dispatch, preserve stable
application/job identities and persist effect receipts. This gateway does not create
a second runner or complete effects merely because a request was accepted.

The route prefix defaults to `/api/sitekit/management/` and may be configured
identically on browser and server. It covers context/settings/application reads,
versioned save/apply, presentation access, reports, CSV imports, accounts, Meta
connection start, posts and explicit job actions. The existing Meta OAuth callback
is served by the host's actor-bound OAuth endpoint; configure its return URL back
to this workspace. Only HTTPS Meta authorization redirects are accepted. Credentials
and OAuth state remain server-only. Errors expose fixed codes; responses are
`no-store`. Mutations require the exact origin. Body/response limits are 128 KiB
and 1 MiB respectively.

### 3. Use the same bodies in a managed host

The managed host passes its authenticated provider into `ManagementWorkspace`.
Its gateway uses the same operations and returns the same credential-free values.
Premium entitlement, organization/site selection and native execution belong to
that host. Connecting a database under the standalone runner does not constitute
a native managed integration. No automatic standalone fallback exists.

This release prepares the reusable entry; mounting it inside an actual managed
application and implementing that application's native execution facade are separate
integration work. Private compatibility imports can switch only after the public
release actually contains these exports; do not introduce sibling source aliases
or guessed package versions.

## Verification

Settings cards show saved/effective revisions and values independently. Saving
never marks a section applied; apply displays its actual durable status. If another
editor changes the record, local inputs are retained and automatic retries stop.
Review the current saved/effective values, explicitly retain the input or discard
it, then save with a newly reviewed version. Permission and capability failures
suppress writes; the server still authorizes every request. Pending applications
and other-client changes refresh on focus, after commands and every 15 seconds.
Refresh failures disable writes and preserve inputs. Site transitions discard
previous caches and fence old async completions, including mutation callbacks.

Source checkout verification includes `bun run test:management-browser`. Install
Playwright and its Chromium browser for that optional test, or set
`SITEKIT_PLAYWRIGHT_MODULE` to the installed module entry. It starts a loopback host
with real SQLite, signed local test sessions and synthetic effect receipts; it
checks save/apply, conflict recovery, dirty guards, late responses, read-only
admission and both mounts. These fixtures are not a production identity provider
or evidence of live Meta/EAOS acceptance. Unit tests additionally reopen a file DB
and exercise atomic permission revocation. The isolated public archive consumer
verifies the exports and browser stylesheet without private registry credentials.

## Troubleshooting / Common Pitfalls

- A 409 requires review. Never retry with a refreshed version automatically.
- A blocked/unknown apply is not a failed effect and must not be redelivered blindly.
- If reads fail, fix the verified session and grants rather than exposing a second store.
- Saved defaults are not effective policy. Build/measurement/publication ports must
  confirm and consume the exact captured revision before reporting application.
- Grant display is advisory; server and dispatch admission remain mandatory.
  Context and marketing access do not require site-settings read permission;
  each actual settings read remains separately authorized.
- Live login, production cron, actual Meta permissions and native managed-host
  acceptance require the host's deployment and service setup.

---

Canonical guide: https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/guides/standalone-host/
Source: `docs/guides/standalone-host.md`

# Run the Public Standalone Host

## Prerequisites

Use a public release containing `@alneas/sitekit-cloudflare/standalone` and the
`sitekit-standalone` scaffold. Candidate archives are tested before publication;
these instructions do not imply that an unreleased export exists in an older
registry version. Node 24+, npm and a Cloudflare account are sufficient; no private
registry credentials, EAOS subscription or private SDK is required.

The reference combines Workers Static Assets, D1, Access and Cron. Its public
website renders a supplied localized page manifest. The existing common management
screens handle settings, measured reports, spending and social jobs. It does not
replace a CMS document editor. Other static-build hosts retain their own build and
publication receipt adapter; this renderer applies configuration at request time.

For production, prepare a domain, Access application and explicit administrator
subjects. Facebook Pages and linked professional Instagram single-image posts
require a registered Meta application, approved permissions and appropriate
accounts. Actual provider approval and production deployment are separate from
local acceptance.

## Public import

```typescript
import { createStandaloneHost } from '@alneas/sitekit-cloudflare/standalone';
import type { StandaloneConfiguration, StandaloneBindings } from '@alneas/sitekit-cloudflare/standalone';
export const runtime = (config: StandaloneConfiguration, bindings: StandaloneBindings) =>
  createStandaloneHost(config, bindings);
```

## Step-by-Step Implementation

### 1. Create the reference project

Install matching public packages in a bootstrap directory, then run:

```sh
npx sitekit-standalone ./my-site
cd my-site
npm install
```

The scaffold pins both SiteKit dependencies to the exact versions actually
installed in the bootstrap directory. It refuses an existing destination. Its
assets, Worker, configuration, setup and local issuer scripts are copied from the
public package. There are no sibling-checkout aliases or private dependencies.

Edit `sitekit.config.json`: immutable deployment origin and tenant/site identity,
initial settings, collection start, installed localized pages and Access issuer/
audience. Initial values import existing configuration when adopting a site;
never reset existing business settings to the sample defaults. Replace the local
administrator subject for production. Verified `/admin/identity` shows the Access
subject without granting that subject site access.

### 2. Initialize local storage and a signed development login

```sh
npm run db:local
npm run dev:identity
```

Keep the identity process running. In a second terminal:

```sh
npm run dev
```

Open the loopback login URL printed by the identity process. It signs an RS256
assertion, sets an HttpOnly cookie and redirects to the local `/admin`. The Worker
still verifies signature, issuer, audience, expiry, issued-at and subject; an email
header alone cannot authenticate. Local keys, encryption material, SQL replay file
and database state are ignored by Git and excluded from the public template.
The Worker rejects local issuer keys on public origins.

Local setup writes first-install saved settings and explicit human/service grants.
It does not invent applied state. Sign in and apply the initial settings sections.
The public page becomes available after site and localization are activated.
Retried setup reuses its saved SQL; changed setup configuration requires an explicit
migration/grant operation. Existing settings or revoked grants are not reset.

### 3. Observe actual settings application

The renderer consumes applied site identity, canonical URL and locale routing.
Only locales present in the installed page artifact can be activated. Prefix
`never` supports one locale in this reference; choose another prefix strategy for
multiple locales. Unsupported application is definitively rejected, preserving
the previously active target. Saving any section leaves the target unchanged.

An apply command captures the exact saved value. The runner atomically activates a
read-only runtime projection and records a durable effect receipt, fenced by source
application, aggregate version, owner epoch and live runner admission. The shared
settings service confirms that receipt. If interrupted between activation and
confirmation, restart confirms the existing receipt without reactivating it.
The projection is an execution target, never a second editable settings store.

Measurement intake checks the activated enabled flag on every request. The supplied
collector refreshes consent mode/lifetime and stops its old collector after policy
changes. Its consent panel still honors browser privacy signals. Retention uses the
activated day count in the scheduled purge; applying retention does not synchronously
delete history. Reports retain the common attribution/minor-currency contract.
Changing currency or timezone does not convert money or move queued UTC jobs.

### 4. Connect Meta and scheduled execution

Add an operator-owned `meta` object to `sitekit.config.json` with `appId`, a supported
`apiVersion`, the application's required `permissions`, and `allowedMediaOrigins`.
Configure the registered HTTPS callback as
`/api/sitekit/management/oauth/callback` on the deployment. Store
`META_APP_SECRET`, `SITEKIT_CURRENT_KEY_ID`, and `SITEKIT_SECRET_KEYS` as Worker
secrets. The last is a JSON map from key IDs to base64-encoded 32-byte AES keys.
Keep previous keys available during rotation. Never place secrets in browser
configuration or commit local secret files.

The Meta feature remains unavailable until configuration and secrets exist. Use
SNS connection in the common screen, save the automatic-publication destinations
and approval policy, then apply them. There is no editable second rule in the
social store. Account credentials are AES-GCM encrypted with tenant/site/account
associated data and never returned to the browser.

The reference exports a real `scheduled` handler and a one-minute Cron. It applies
pending settings, processes due posts and purges expired measurement records under
a separate service grant. Human administrator JWTs cannot acquire `publish`, `run`
or trusted completion rights. Concurrent invocations claim each destination through
CAS; persisted checkpoints precede visible dispatch. Unknown publication outcomes
stop automatic resend and require reconciliation.

For local scheduled acceptance, Wrangler's local scheduled endpoint can trigger the
actual handler. That development endpoint belongs to the local runtime; the
application exposes no anonymous HTTP cron endpoint. Production Cron registration
and deployment require the operator's separate infrastructure action.

### 5. Connect successful content publication

Inside the same trusted server, call `host.published(event)` only after publication
succeeds. An external CMS/build hook can use the HMAC endpoint:

```typescript
import { createStandalonePublicationRequest } from '@alneas/sitekit-cloudflare/standalone';
import type { PublicationEvent } from '@alneas/sitekit-cloudflare/standalone';
export async function notify(event: PublicationEvent, serverKey: Uint8Array) {
  const request = await createStandalonePublicationRequest(
    'https://example.test/api/sitekit/publication', event, serverKey,
  );
  return fetch(request);
}
```

Configure the same base64 32-byte `SITEKIT_PUBLICATION_KEY` in the Worker. Missing or
invalid signatures deny access. Live publisher grants and authority are checked
again after the five-minute signature envelope. First admission captures
publication data, destinations and approval requirements. Repeating the same content
revision cannot acquire destinations from a later rule; changed content under the
same revision conflicts. Disabled events remain disabled on replay. The notification
only proposes jobs; the scheduled handler performs delivery.

### 6. Prepare production explicitly

Set the real D1 ID and deployment origin in configuration. Protect `/admin*` and
`/api/sitekit/management/*` with Access while keeping the website and consented
analytics intake public. The Worker independently verifies the assertions, including
when an alternate route bypasses the Access edge. `run_worker_first` protects admin
assets before Static Assets can serve them. Use exact configured origin for mutations.
Set verified administrator subjects, service grants and secret keys before use.

Run `npm run typegen`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm run deploy:check`. A dry run does
not deploy or prove remote grants, callbacks or Cron delivery. Initializing remote
storage, changing grants and deployment are explicit operator actions; local setup
never performs them implicitly. Enable logs/traces as supplied; log only safe status
metadata and never OAuth URLs, tokens or publication text.

## Verification

`bun run test:standalone` in the source checkout creates a fresh npm-only consumer
of the exact candidate archives, checks the packaged scaffold, builds assets,
initializes local D1, generates Worker types and runs Wrangler's dry run. It then
uses Wrangler's own Workers runtime and persistent D1 for verified JWT login,
protected assets, settings save/apply/render, encrypted OAuth, Facebook/Instagram
Cron delivery and restart without resend. Set `SITEKIT_PLAYWRIGHT_MODULE` to run the
browser interaction acceptance as well.

The external issuer keys and Meta HTTP responses in acceptance are local fixtures.
They exercise the production verifier and delivery protocol but do not establish
actual Access policy, Meta permission approval, deployed scheduling or a real post.
The ordinary unit gates cover stale authority/grants, conflict and unknown-result
semantics. Storage bounds remain explicit: at most 20 accounts, 500 social jobs and
publication receipts per site, with 512 KiB social state; shared settings have their
own documented command/history capacity. Capacity failures never silently evict
replay identities. Plan explicit archival/migration before exceeding those bounds.

## Troubleshooting / Common Pitfalls

- A settings save is not an application. Check the section's actual receipt/state.
- A stopped/revoked runner leaves pending work visible; it never changes execution owner.
- A 409 requires explicit review, not an automatic version refresh and overwrite.
- Invalid signatures and audience/issuer mismatches deny login even with identity headers.
- Keep the AES rotation key that encrypted existing accounts until they are re-encrypted.
- Local signed login is for loopback development; use actual Access on a public host.
- Meta media must be reachable from approved HTTPS origins. Use live provider setup
  acceptance before production publishing.

See [Shared Management Settings](https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/guides/management-settings/) and
[Embed the Shared Management Console](https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/guides/management-console/) for the shared contracts.
Cloudflare documents [Access JWT verification](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/applications/http-apps/authorization-cookie/validating-json/),
[Worker-first asset routing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/routing/worker-script/)
and [Cron handlers](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/configuration/cron-triggers/).

The reference Wrangler configuration sets `observability.redact_query_string: true`. Preserve this setting in custom hosts: Meta OAuth exchanges contain credentials in query parameters, and automatic request/fetch telemetry must redact those parameters. Do not log OAuth request URLs, authorization codes, or tokens yourself.

---

Canonical guide: https://tech-docs.alneas.com/sitekit/docs/guides/managed-execution/
Source: `docs/guides/managed-execution.md`

# Connect a Managed Execution Authority

## Prerequisites

Use a release containing `createManagedSiteRuntime` from
`@alneas/sitekit-cloudflare/management`. Candidate archives are tested separately;
older registry versions do not acquire unreleased exports automatically. The host
owns verified human/service sessions, current subscription and site/action grants,
transactional persistence, exact settings activation and encrypted Meta credentials.
Public connector availability does not grant access to a licensed service.

The shared components and `createManagementHttpProvider` do not change. A connected
screen calls the managed API as its sole authority; no local fallback database or
publisher is created. Navigation embedding and connect/disconnect transfer are
separate operations, not consequences of selecting a different URL.

## Public import

```typescript
import {createManagedSiteRuntime} from '@alneas/sitekit-cloudflare/management';
import type {ManagedSiteOptions} from '@alneas/sitekit-cloudflare/management';
export const connect = (options:ManagedSiteOptions) => createManagedSiteRuntime(options);
```

## Step-by-Step Implementation

### 1. Bind one authenticated workspace

Derive tenant, site, actor, principal kind and authority epoch from the verified host
session and registered site. Never accept identity, premium flags, service roles,
stores, factories or credentials from browser JSON. Resolve a new server composition
for each request; it is intentionally tied to the admission generation and epoch.
The runtime rejects non-EAOS, paused, foreign-scope and changed-epoch records.

Provide `authorize(operation, accountId?)` for the actual current subscription,
lifecycle and resource policy. It returns an opaque permission generation. Every
relevant control change must advance that generation. Both reads/replays and writes
check admission; capability and permission fields are presentation only. Service-only
`run`, `publish`, `publication`, `ingest`, `outcome` and `completeApplication` rights
cannot be acquired by a human runtime, even if a host accidentally grants the names.

### 2. Supply native persistence and real activation

`settingsStore` persists one canonical settings aggregate. Its compare-and-swap must
check source version, authority epoch and the bound actor's current permission
generation atomically. The social store similarly fences its revision, authority
and admission generation. A preflight permission callback alone is insufficient;
use a transaction with the native control store or an equivalent all-instance drain.

Saving remains inactive. Applying reserves an immutable section revision. The
service runner passes that captured value to `activation.apply`, and completion
requires `activation.verify` to confirm an existing matching target receipt. Resume
existing receipts without executing the target twice. Unknown external build or
provider results remain pending; do not invent a successful receipt. External static
build hosts must supply their actual build/publication receipt adapter.

### 3. Connect canonical measurement and encrypted social ports

`measurement(effective)` provides the common marketing services using the applied
retention and other runtime policy. Confirm its returned tenant/site exactly match.
The authority must admit native measurement writes in the same transaction as its
control generation. Keep integer minor amounts, last-non-direct attribution,
consent filtering, immutable dedupe and coverage semantics; unrelated native report
models must not be presented as equivalent by renaming fields.

Optional `social(context)` constructs the owning native social service with the
verified actor, live admission and applied publication policy. Its native service
owns queue, approvals, dispatch/reconciliation and effect receipts; public OAuth,
`SecretBox` and provider protocol helpers can be injected without a second queue. `createMetaOAuth`, `createMetaDeliveryDriver` and `createSecretBox` are
server-only helpers exported by the same adapter entry. The managed service uses
the applied site origin and publication policy. Credentials never enter the public
provider. Configure `observability.redact_query_string: true` when using Workers
telemetry: Meta OAuth exchanges contain query credentials. Other hosts must provide
equivalent redaction and must never log OAuth URLs or provider secrets.

### 4. Use the existing common HTTP client

After verifying its actual user session, the host calls `runtime.fetch(request)`.
That runtime is an authenticated port, not a standalone anonymous request listener.
Use a distinct trusted service runtime for `run`, `published`, `ingest` and `outcome`;
there is no browser completion or scheduled-run route.

```typescript
import {createManagementHttpProvider} from '@alneas/sitekit/management/http';
export const provider = createManagementHttpProvider({
  origin:'https://console.example.test',
  basePath:'/api/sites/example/management/',
});
```

Point the existing `ManagementWorkspace` or `ManagementApp` at this provider and
include the common stylesheet. Both shells observe the same saved/effective
revisions. A 409 requires review/reload; transports never refresh versions and retry
writes automatically. Confirm OAuth through the authenticated host callback using
`runtime.completeConnect`, then redirect to a fixed registered management URL.

## Verification

Exercise the installed public client against the actual native store/API: saved
versus applied values and target output, stale writes, current read-only permissions,
revoked subscription/site access, canonical event/spending reports, encrypted OAuth,
concurrent schedulers and restart without resend. Fake provider HTTP and local
fixtures establish protocol/persistence behavior, not live account acceptance.
Private authority implementation and operational instructions stay in their owner.

## Troubleshooting / Common Pitfalls

A 403 after a subscription or site-grant change is expected; refresh the verified
host session and resolve a new runtime rather than falling back to local storage.
A 409 on save/apply requires reviewing the current saved/effective revisions.
An application remaining `applying` needs its actual native target receipt; a
successful request enqueue alone is insufficient. Missing social configuration is
reported unavailable, and a provider's unknown dispatch requires reconciliation.
An unsupported database dialect needs a deliberate canonical-semantic adapter;
do not change the report model or bypass transactional admission to make it run.

## Shared embedding and connection recovery

The public `ManagementWorkspace` is the screen body for a verified enclosing host;
`ManagementApp` adds the standalone shell. Pass the same provider and stylesheet.
Forward `onDirtyChange` to the host's site selector and guard site switches while
inputs or operations are pending. Replace the binding on principal, site or epoch
changes, and immediately remove the old workspace on logout. Host organization,
subscription and site-list navigation stays outside this body.

The optional `ManagementConsoleProvider.connection` supplies status, plan and
advance commands. `createManagementHttpProvider` uses the same `connection/status`,
`connection/plan` and `connection/advance` routes in either host. A server provider
must independently authorize connection administration on every command, including
idempotent replays. The common gateway verifies the session, bound site and Origin;
connection administration is an additional service permission, never implied by
ordinary read access. Status contains owner, phase, counts and permission only.
The browser never receives snapshots, permits, tokens or peer endpoints.

Use `createConnectionContext` for a recovery-only bootstrap when the current host
cannot expose business settings during cutover. Its settings and marketing
permissions are denied. The shared connection page remains available so a reload
can resume the same transfer. Do not manufacture applied business values from a
local stale snapshot to make bootstrap succeed.

## Controlled connect and disconnect

Provision the stable site-local authority store before enabling a connection, using
`authoritySchemaSql`, `createAuthorityRecord`, `initializeAuthority` and
`createD1AuthorityStore`. Initialization preserves an existing owner. The control
record is separate from settings: it contains only the execution fence, transfer
receipts and durable permit identities. It remains at the stable site endpoint
throughout both directions of migration. The permission-generation admission row
must change atomically with the actor's grants.

Compose `createAuthorityService` with explicit trusted peers. A plan chooses the
configured opposite owner; it never accepts a URL or tenant from browser input.
Advance closes admissions, drains durable permits, freezes the source, validates
and stages the destination, commits a fresh owner/epoch, then activates the staged
state. Owner activation is idempotent by transfer ID and epoch. If activation loses
its response, resume that phase. Once ownership is committed, never roll it back
or let the previous scheduler take over on a timeout. If an admitted operation
changes the source after planning, drain it and capture its final inventory before
freezing; the transfer preserves the latest committed business state.

Every instance that writes or executes effects must use the same control channel.
`createAuthorityExecutor` holds a durable permit around its operation. Thrown or
uncertain work stays unresolved; elapsed time never resolves it. Its trusted proof
port must attest a durable result, and the service's `verifyPermit` must verify that
proof against the exact operation. Neither port has an allow-all default. A known
rollback may be resolved as `not-executed` only with verified evidence. Use
`createAuthorityDeliveryDriver` around each external SNS attempt; retain its exact
attempt ID for reconciliation. Reconciliation resolves that attempt without a new
publish, including while admissions are closing. Unknown effects block cutover.

The standalone host's optional `authority` binding connects the safe browser
controls, executor and authenticated EAOS delegation ports. Before connecting,
configure it on **all** serving and scheduled instances. The delegation must map a
verified local principal to an authorized EAOS principal through a trusted server
channel; request JSON or forwarded user/role headers are not identity evidence.
EAOS independently rechecks its current contract and site rights. The host relays
management, telemetry, effective runtime settings and publication notifications to
the current EAOS owner. Local Cron skips execution after EAOS owns the site.
Authority-channel or EAOS failures fail closed without switching owners. A host
that has participated in migration refuses operation if its authority binding is
later omitted. Initial standalone use requires no EAOS connection or private SDK.

## Snapshot adapters and retained history

`createSiteTransferPeer` supplies bounded, resumable staging over native business
ports. `createD1TransferArchive` encrypts every persisted page and receipt with
scope/owner/transfer associated data. Credentials are decrypted and re-encrypted
only through a trusted target sealing port, and the manifest binds their semantic
content without depending on randomized ciphertext. Target activation requires the
stable control's matching owner, epoch, transfer ID and ready receipt. An inactive
predecessor is reusable only when its retained recovery inventory is unchanged;
a divergent destination is rejected rather than merged or overwritten.

For the standard host, provision `transferBusinessSchemaSql` and use
`createStandaloneTransferData`. The standard bootstrap includes these tables.
The native owner supplies its own transactional settings, SNS and SQL adapters;
its SNS service continues to own delivery and workflow receipts. Preserve canonical
job IDs, approvals, schedules, request keys, publication fingerprints, attempts,
provider checkpoints and remote IDs. Preserve original native provenance alongside
canonical projections. Snapshot pause/adoption and their receipts must commit in
the same business transaction, and retries must consult those receipts.

Transfer raw measurement fingerprints/write identities, spend/outcome rows, privacy
revocations and original collection coverage. Destination retention uses actually
applied settings and the imported collection start. Saved drafts remain separate
from effective values; activate only the imported effective values in actual native
targets. An applying settings request, unresolved provider result or active OAuth
handshake blocks migration. Existing session-bound OAuth handshakes cannot move
between hosts. Current bounded transfer limits are 50,000 records / 8 MiB total,
with paged encrypted persistence; exceeding a limit rejects the transfer without
truncation. Use operator-managed offline migration for larger inventories.
